[2473] COGNITIVE SCIENCE AND THEORY OF COMMUNICATION Master's Degree Course in English

-----

Below is a **structured, concise summary** of the key information from the Italian academic document, organized for clarity and practical use. It covers **degree paths, core competencies, career roles, and workplace functions** for graduates in **Cognitive Sciences (LM-55)** and **Communication Theories (LM-92)**, including the integrated "interclass" approach.

---

### **1. Degree Paths & Core Focus**
| **Program**               | **LM-55 (Cognitive Sciences)**                          | **LM-92 (Communication Theories)**                      |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| **Core Focus**            | Cognitive/neuroscientific foundations, AI, human-computer interfaces, rehabilitation. | Communication theory, media strategy, ethics, digital/social communication. |
| **Key Skills Acquired**   | - Cognitive rehabilitation & linguistics<br>- AI programming & interface design<br>- Neuroscientific research<br>- Cognitive ergonomics (multimedia communication) | - Philosophical/linguistic theories of communication<br>- Media tech & digital platforms (social media, web, TV, radio)<br>- Ethical/psychological aspects of communication<br>- Critical analysis of advertising/public communication |
| **Research Methods**      | Experimental cognitive studies, neuroscientific analysis, AI modeling. | Critical analysis of communication channels, social context analysis, multimedia content design. |

---

### **2. "Interclass" Advantage (Combined Pathway)**
Graduates **bridge both fields**, enabling:
- **Original application** of cognitive science to communication design (e.g., user-friendly interfaces, cognitive ergonomics in media).
- **Cross-sector adaptability**: Work in both *cognitive research* (e.g., rehabilitation) and *communication strategy* (e.g., e-government, media production).
- **Advanced research readiness**: Preparation for PhDs, master’s, or specialized training (e.g., cognitive ergonomics, AI ethics).

---

### **3. Professional Roles & Workplace Functions**
#### **A. Cognitive Sciences Graduates (LM-55)**
| **Role**                                  | **Workplace Context**                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cognitive Rehabilitation Specialist**    | Public/private clinics, schools, rehabilitation centers (theoretical + practical application). |
| **AI/Interface Designer**                  | Tech companies, R&D labs (designing software, automated systems, human-computer interfaces). |
| **Cognitive Research Lead**                | Universities, research institutes (e.g., cognitive ergonomics for multimedia platforms). |
| **Service Director (Public/Private)**      | Public administration, corporate HR, community services (managing person/group-focused services). |

#### **B. Communication Theories Graduates (LM-92)**
| **Role**                                  | **Workplace Context**                                                                 |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Strategic Communication Manager**      | Media companies, PR firms, advertising agencies (designing integrated communication environments for web, TV, radio). |
| **E-Government Specialist**               | Public institutions (ministries, courts, universities, local authorities) – implementing transparent digital services. |
| **Multimedia Content Designer**           | Private/public media (e.g., thematic content for web platforms, digital publishing). |
| **Communication Ethics Advisor**         | Organizations needing ethical frameworks for information dissemination (e.g., social media, crisis communication). |

#### **C. "Interclass" Graduates (Combined Expertise)**
- **Work in hybrid roles**: e.g., designing **cognitive-friendly interfaces** for e-government platforms (combining cognitive science + communication strategy).
- **Lead cross-functional teams**: In tech firms or public institutions requiring both *user experience (UX) research* and *communication strategy*.
- **Innovate in emerging fields**: AI-driven communication tools, ethical AI in media, cognitive accessibility for digital services.

---

### **4. Key Differentiators vs. Traditional Programs**
| **Aspect**                | **Traditional Programs**                          | **This Interclass Program**                                  |
|---------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Scope**                 | Narrow focus (e.g., *only* cognitive science *or* *only* communication). | **Integrated approach**: Cognitive science + communication theory. |
| **Career Flexibility**    | Limited to one sector (e.g., rehab *or* media).  | **Transversal skills**: Apply to tech, public admin, media, healthcare. |
| **Innovation Edge**       | Reactive application of existing methods.        | **Proactive innovation**: Designing solutions using *both* cognitive insights *and* communication strategy (e.g., reducing user cognitive load in e-government apps). |

---

### **5. Why This Program Stands Out**
- **Solves real-world gaps**: Most programs don’t connect *how the brain processes information* (cognitive science) with *how to communicate effectively* (communication theory).
- **High-demand skills**: 
  - **Cognitive ergonomics** (designing intuitive digital services) is critical for e-government and tech companies.
  - **Ethical communication** is increasingly mandated in digital policy (e.g., EU AI Act).
- **Career trajectory**: Graduates move from **specialist roles** (e.g., AI designer) to **leadership** (e.g., directing cognitive communication teams in public institutions).

> 💡 **In short**: This program trains **future-proof professionals** who don’t just *use* technology but *design it with human cognition in mind* – making them indispensable in tech, public service, and media.

COURSE: [2445] PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES

[2445] PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

### Summary: **Laurea in Scienze e Tecniche Psicologiche (Bachelor’s in Psychological Sciences and Techniques)**  
*Italy’s 3-Year First-Cycle Psychology Program*  

#### **Key Overview**  
- **Degree Title**: *Tecnico in Scienze Psicologiche* (Psychological Sciences Technician).  
- **Level**: Bachelor’s (Laurea Triennale), **not sufficient** for independent practice as a psychologist.  
- **Next Step**: Requires a **Master’s (Laurea Magistrale)** to become a fully licensed *Psicologo* (Sezione A of the professional register).  
- **Work Authorization**: After completing a **practical internship (tirocinio pratico valutativo)** and registering with **Sezione B** of the *Albo Professionale degli Psicologi*, graduates may work **under supervision** in specific roles.  

---

#### **Career Path & Scope of Practice**  
Graduates (with Sezione B registration) can collaborate with Master’s-level psychologists (*Sezione A*) in:  
1. **Multidisciplinary Teams**:  
   - Assessing needs/disabilities (e.g., for rehabilitation, social integration).  
   - Supporting family dynamics (e.g., parent-child relationships, caregiver burden).  
2. **Intervention Roles**:  
   - Conducting psychological assessments using standardized tools (e.g., cognitive, behavioral, social evaluations).  
   - Assisting in educational, health-promotion, and risk-behavior modification programs.  
   - Contributing to rehabilitation for individuals with disabilities, neuropsychological deficits, or substance dependence.  
3. **Data & Tool Support**:  
   - Analyzing data for psychodiagnostic reports (under supervision).  
   - Adapting psychological assessment tools (e.g., surveys, tests).  

**❌ Cannot**: Practice independently, diagnose psychiatric conditions, or lead clinical interventions without a Master’s degree.  

---

#### **Core Competencies Developed**  
- **Technical Skills**:  
  - Administering psychological assessments (e.g., cognitive, behavioral tools).  
  - Statistical analysis and research methodology.  
- **Soft Skills**:  
  - Teamwork, emotional regulation, active listening, and intercultural communication.  
  - Problem-solving, risk/resilience identification, and ethical decision-making.  
- **Critical Thinking**:  
  - Evaluating neuroscientific/clinical literature and applying critical analysis.  

---

#### **Program Requirements**  
- **Language**: Instruction and exams in **Italian** (no English required).  
- **Learning Outcomes**:  
  - **Autonomy**: Critically assess theories and research limitations.  
  - **Communication**: Explain psychological concepts clearly (in Italian) and use multimedia for data presentation.  
  - **Lifelong Learning**: Self-directed updates on psychological science advancements.  
- **Verification**:  
  - Written/oral exams, research projects, and internship reports.  

---

#### **Important Notes**  
- **European Alignment**: Follows Bologna Process standards but aligns with Italy’s specific professional framework.  
- **Professional Path**:  
  - **Bachelor’s (Sezione B)**: Supervised support roles (e.g., in schools, social services, rehabilitation centers).  
  - **Master’s (Sezione A)**: Independent practice (e.g., clinical psychology, private practice).  
- **No Full Licensure**: The Bachelor’s alone does **not** grant the title *Psicologo*; a Master’s is mandatory.  

---

#### **Why This Matters**  
This program prepares students for **entry-level roles** in psychology-related fields (e.g., education, social services) while emphasizing foundational skills. It serves as a **stepping stone** to a Master’s, which is required for clinical or independent practice in Italy. Graduates must prioritize completing a Master’s to advance their career.  

*For international students: This degree is valid in Italy but may not align with certification systems in other countries (e.g., U.S. or EU). Always verify local requirements.*  

---  
*Source: Italian Ministry of Education, Professional Register (Albo degli Psicologi), and Bologna Process standards.*

[2457] TOURISM, CULTURE AND BUSINESS SCIENCES Bachelor's Degree Program

-----

### Summary of the **"Scienze del Turismo, della Cultura e dell'Impresa" (L15) Bachelor's Program**  

This **first-cycle (L15) degree program** prepares students for **interdisciplinary careers in tourism, cultural heritage management, and tourism-oriented business operations**. It combines **humanities, economics, and practical skills** to address the evolving demands of the tourism sector, emphasizing **sustainability, cultural preservation, and technological innovation**.  

---

#### **Core Focus Areas**  
1. **Tourism & Cultural Valorization**:  
   - Designing cultural itineraries, managing heritage sites, and promoting territorial identity.  
   - Preparing students for the **official tourism guide certification** (examination eligibility).  
2. **Economic & Business Management**:  
   - Strategic planning for tourism enterprises (hotels, travel agencies, event management).  
   - Marketing, financial tools, and sustainable business models.  
3. **Sustainability & Technology**:  
   - Integrating eco-friendly practices and digital tools (e.g., IT, multimedia) into tourism strategies.  

---

#### **Key Learning Outcomes**  
| **Competency**               | **Description**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Critical Thinking (III)**  | Analyze tourism challenges through interdisciplinary lenses (e.g., cultural vs. economic). |
| **Communication (IV)**       | Fluent in **2+ EU languages** + Italian; skilled in written/visual communication (reports, presentations, infographics). |
| **Technical Skills (V)**     | Proficiency in IT, data analysis, and modern tourism technologies (e.g., digital marketing, CRM systems). |
| **Autonomy (III)**           | Develop solutions balancing tradition, technology, and sustainability.          |

---

#### **Professional Roles**  
Graduates work as:  
- **Tourism Promoters** (marketing cultural destinations).  
- **Cultural Site Managers** (heritage preservation, visitor experience design).  
- **Business Managers** for tourism enterprises (hotels, event agencies, travel startups).  
- **Public-Private Liaisons** (coordinating government and businesses for tourism development).  

---

#### **Program Structure**  
- **Curricula-Based**: Specialized tracks (e.g., cultural tourism, business management).  
- **Practical Training**:  
  - **Internships** (curricular, in tourism businesses or cultural institutions).  
  - **Laboratories** (e.g., itinerary design, digital marketing simulations).  
- **Language & Tech Focus**:  
  - Mandatory **2+ EU languages** (e.g., English, French, Spanish).  
  - Digital tools training (social media, data visualization, booking systems).  

---

#### **Unique Value Proposition**  
- **Interdisciplinary Blend**: Merges **humanities** (history, anthropology) with **business economics**.  
- **Sustainability-Driven**: Prioritizes eco-tourism and cultural preservation.  
- **Global Readiness**: Prepares students for international tourism markets via multilingual and tech skills.  

---

#### **Why This Program?**  
Italy’s **rich cultural/natural heritage** and **high tourism demand** create urgent need for professionals who bridge **cultural storytelling**, **business acumen**, and **sustainable practices**. Graduates are equipped to lead in a sector where **digital transformation** and **cultural sensitivity** are key to success.  

*Note: All teaching and assessments are conducted in **Italian** (L15 degree standard).*

Here is a concise, professional English summary of the Italian DAMS (Diploma in Arts Management and Cultural Heritage) program description, structured for clarity and key takeaways:

---

### **Program Overview**  
**Degree:** DAMS (Diploma in Arts Management and Cultural Heritage)  
**Focus:** Comprehensive training in managing performing arts (theater, cinema, music, visual arts) and cultural institutions, emphasizing **practical application**, **interdisciplinary methodology** (Performance Studies), and **local industry integration**.  

---

### **Key Features**  
1. **Unique Local Partnerships**  
   - **Cinema:** Collaboration with *Fondazione Horcynus Orca* (Taormina Arte Festival, Salina Doc Fest) and a dedicated film school.  
   - **Music:** Partnership with *Conservatorio di Messina* for integrated teaching.  
   - **Theater:** Direct engagement with high-profile local artisans and venues.  
   - **Museums:** Practical training in museum space animation.  

2. **Methodology**  
   - **Performance Studies** as core framework, linking artistic practices to socio-cultural contexts.  
   - **Hybrid Communication Skills:** Mastery of verbal (2+ EU languages + professional Italian) and non-verbal (graphic design, data visualization, multimedia) communication.  

3. **Curriculum Structure**  
   - **Theory + Practice:** Lectures, workshops, and **mandatory internships** (cinema school, theaters, festivals).  
   - **Interdisciplinary Courses:** Integrates *L-ART/05* (Performing Arts), *L-FIL-LET/11* (Literature), and *M-DEA/01* (Media).  

---

### **Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors)**  
| **Descriptor**               | **Key Competencies**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **I. Knowledge & Understanding** | • Historical-cultural analysis of artistic practices.<br>• Ability to "read" performances *emically* (internally).<br>• Critical engagement with artistic heritage. |
| **II. Application**          | • Organizing/curating events (theater, film, music).<br>• Programming seasons, festivals, and multimedia productions.<br>• Managing theaters, museums, and cultural institutions. |
| **III. Critical Judgment**   | • Adapting to socio-economic challenges in the arts sector (e.g., Sicily’s context).<br>• Identifying opportunities amid resource constraints. |
| **IV. Communication**        | • Presenting ideas in multiple languages/media (e.g., film, infographics, live critique).<br>• Tailoring communication to diverse audiences (curators, producers, public). |
| **V. Learning Ability**      | • Rapid adaptation to evolving artistic forms (e.g., digital media, hybrid genres like *docu-fiction*). |

---

### **Career Paths**  
Graduates become **specialists in cultural management**, equipped for roles such as:  
- **Event Curators** (theater, film festivals, museums).  
- **Program Managers** (theaters, conservatories, cultural institutions).  
- **Multimedia Producers** (music, cinema, digital content).  
- **Cultural Critics & Educators** (theater/literature specialists).  
- **Museum Animators** (designing interactive exhibits).  
- **Media Liaisons** (radio, TV, digital platforms).  

---

### **Distinctive Strengths**  
- **Sicilian Context:** Leverages unique local assets (Taormina Arte Festival, conservatory partnerships) to address industry challenges.  
- **Hybrid Skills:** Combines *artistic expertise* (e.g., film/music production) with *management* (budgeting, promotion, digital strategy).  
- **EU Alignment:** Meets Dublin Descriptor standards for employability in Europe’s cultural sector.  
- **Industry Integration:** 100% of curriculum includes **practical projects** (e.g., working with *Fondazione Horcynus Orca*).  

---

### **Why This Program Stands Out**  
> *"It bridges the gap between academic theory and the real-world demands of Sicily’s vibrant but resource-constrained arts ecosystem, training graduates to innovate within constraints while leveraging local cultural heritage."*  

This program is designed not just to teach management, but to cultivate **adaptive leaders** who can navigate the complexities of modern cultural production—from traditional theaters to digital media—using Sicily’s unique artistic landscape as a laboratory.  

---  
*Note: "DAMS" is specific to Italian higher education (Diploma in Arts Management). The program aligns with the European Higher Education Area (EHEA) via Dublin Descriptors.*

### Overview of the "Scienze della Formazione e della Comunicazione" Program (Italy)  
This interdisciplinary program combines **pedagogy, communication sciences, and digital technologies**, offering two specialized tracks at graduation:  
- **L-19 (Educatore socio-pedagogico e dell’infanzia)**  
- **L-20 (Scienze della comunicazione)**  

---

### **Core Competencies**  
All graduates develop **interdisciplinary skills** in:  
- **Cultural fields**: Pedagogy, philosophy, sociology, semiotics, psychology.  
- **Technological fields**: Digital communication tools, multimedia design, network resources.  
- **Social engagement**: Ability to address challenges like multiculturalism, disability, ecological deficits, and social marginalization.  

---

### **Specialization Tracks**  

#### **1. L-19: Socio-Pedagogical Educator for Early Childhood (Ages 0–3)**  
**Focus**:  
- Early childhood development, socio-pedagogical support, and inclusive education.  
- Tailored interventions for children with sensory, social, or cognitive disabilities.  
- Promoting diversity and preventing social disadvantage through education.  

**Professional Roles**:  
- **Early childhood educator** in childcare centers, family support services, and socio-educational programs.  
- **Socio-pedagogical coordinator** in community projects, multicultural settings, or social inclusion initiatives.  
- **Specialist in developmental disorders** (e.g., autism, learning disabilities) for educational planning.  

**Key Skills**:  
- Child-centered pedagogy, family engagement, play-based learning, and trauma-informed practices.  

---

#### **2. L-20: Communication Sciences & Media Expert**  
**Focus**:  
- Digital communication strategies, multimedia content creation, and media analysis.  
- Application of technology in public/private communication (e.g., PR, digital campaigns, cultural content).  

**Professional Roles**:  
- **Communication strategist** for public institutions, NGOs, or private companies.  
- **Multimedia content designer** (e.g., social media, educational apps, interactive platforms).  
- **Media analyst** for local/regional/national organizations managing information flows.  

**Key Skills**:  
- Advanced use of digital tools (e.g., data visualization, video editing, social media analytics).  
- Cross-cultural communication and crisis management in media.  

---

### **Learning Outcomes (Key Graduate Attributes)**  
1. **Knowledge**: Mastery of pedagogical, psychological, and communication theories.  
2. **Communication**: Ability to explain projects clearly (e.g., educational plans, media campaigns) using multimedia tools (presentations, infographics, videos).  
3. **Adaptability**: Respond to evolving social needs (e.g., digital transformation, migration, sustainability).  
4. **Digital Literacy**: Proficiency in leveraging online resources and emerging technologies.  
5. **Ethical Practice**: Prioritizing human-centered approaches in education and communication.  

---

### **Language & Professional Context**  
- **Language of instruction**: **Italian** (all exams and coursework).  
- **Workplace settings**:  
  - **L-19**: Schools, childcare centers, social services, cultural associations.  
  - **L-20**: PR agencies, government communications, media production, NGOs.  

---

### **Why This Program?**  
- **Unique blend**: Merges **education** (L-19) with **digital communication** (L-20), addressing modern demands for integrated, tech-savvy professionals.  
- **Social impact**: Prepares graduates to tackle challenges like inequality, digital exclusion, and inclusive education.  
- **Career flexibility**: Both tracks open doors to public, private, and nonprofit sectors.  

*Note: Graduates must demonstrate proficiency in Italian for academic and professional contexts.*  

---  
This program equips students to become **innovative leaders** in education and communication, blending theory with practical, technology-driven solutions for contemporary society. 🌐📚💡

COURSE: [2449] CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY AND HEALTH IN THE LIFE CYCLE (ENABLING THE PROFESSION OF PSYCHOLOGIST)
CURRICULUM: General Description
SECTION: General Description
URL: https://unime.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10611

Master's Degree Course

-----

**Summary: Bachelor's in Clinical and Health Psychology Across the Lifespan**  

This program prepares graduates to work in **clinical and health psychology**, emphasizing a **lifespan approach** (from childhood to old age) and **evidence-based practices**. Graduates develop competencies in:  
- **Autonomy of Judgment**: Critically assessing individual, family, and contextual factors; making ethical, evidence-driven decisions; and managing complex psychological challenges.  
- **Communication**: Effectively engaging with clients, interdisciplinary teams, and stakeholders through oral and written reports (e.g., psychological evaluations, intervention plans).  
- **Lifelong Learning**: Continuously updating skills via scientific literature, professional collaboration, and reflective practice.  
- **Professional Skills**: Conducting **multidimensional psychological diagnostics** (e.g., cognitive, emotional, relational), designing **preventive, therapeutic, and rehabilitative interventions**, and working in **multidisciplinary teams** (e.g., with medical professionals).  

**Professional Scope** (post-registration with the *Ordine degli Psicologi*):  
- Deliver **psychological support, prevention, and well-being promotion** across all life domains (social, professional, daily life) in **public/private institutions**.  
- Perform **psychodiagnostic assessments** focused on psychosocial distress.  
- Lead **multidisciplinary interventions** for individuals, couples, families, and communities.  
- Provide **consultation, expert opinions (peritia), supervision, training, and rehabilitation services**.  

**Key Requirements**:  
- Completion of a **practical evaluation internship (TPV)** and **final thesis** demonstrating applied skills.  
- **Ethical and deontological adherence** in all professional activities.  
- **Continuous professional development** to address evolving research and societal needs.  

This program equips graduates to address psychological challenges holistically, integrating **cultural, gender, and institutional contexts** while prioritizing **evidence-based outcomes** and **client-centered care**.

[3011] MEDICINE AND SURGERY Master's Degree Single Cycle 6 years

-----

**Medical and Surgery Degree Program with a Biotechnology Focus (LM41)**

**I. Knowledge and Understanding**  
The program aims to train medical doctors with solid scientific knowledge, integrated with biotechnological and engineering expertise essential for practicing medicine in a technologically advanced society. Graduates will possess comprehensive knowledge of the human body, diseases, treatments, and preventive measures, including the biological, psychological, and social aspects of health and illness. They will understand the principles of biotechnology, engineering, and digital tools relevant to modern medical practice. This includes knowledge of molecular biology, genetics, bioinformatics, medical devices, and data analysis techniques. Graduates will also be familiar with ethical, legal, and social implications of biotechnology and digital health applications.

**II. Autonomy of Judgment**  
Graduates will be able to:  
1. Apply scientific knowledge to diagnose and treat patients, considering individual differences and social contexts.  
2. Evaluate and select appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic technologies, including digital tools and biotechnological innovations.  
3. Make informed decisions in complex clinical scenarios, balancing evidence-based medicine with patient preferences.  
4. Exercise professional responsibility in patient care and community health, adhering to medical ethics and deontological codes.  
5. Reflect critically on their professional practice, including interactions with patients and colleagues, methods used, and emotional experiences.  
6. Choose and implement suitable hardware and software technologies for patient care, respecting the social and human context of healthcare delivery.

**III. Communication Skills**  
Graduates will be able to:  
1. Listen attentively to understand and synthesize relevant information on health issues.  
2. Communicate clearly and effectively with patients and their families, enabling shared decision-making.  
3. Collaborate efficiently with colleagues, departments, communities, and media.  
4. Work effectively in interdisciplinary teams involving healthcare professionals.  
5. Demonstrate foundational teaching skills and appropriate attitudes toward others.  
6. Show cultural sensitivity to enhance interactions with patients and communities.  
7. Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.  
8. Maintain accurate and comprehensive medical documentation.  
9. Summarize and present information tailored to the audience’s needs, discussing achievable and acceptable action plans for individuals and communities.  
10. Communicate technical expertise with bioengineers, health technology designers, and bioinformaticians to identify optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

**IV. Learning Ability**  
Graduates will develop the capacity for lifelong, self-directed learning, including:  
1. Collecting, organizing, and interpreting health and biomedical information from diverse resources and databases.  
2. Gathering specific patient information from clinical data management systems.  
3. Using information and communication technologies to support diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices, as well as health monitoring.  
4. Understanding the applications and limitations of information technology in healthcare.  
5. Maintaining a well-organized medical practice archive for analysis and improvement.

**V. Professional Competencies**  
**Role in the Work Context**  
Graduates will practice as medical doctors within the framework of European Community regulations, national and regional laws, both within the National Health Service (SSN) and in private or contracted facilities. Their primary objective is to maintain or restore each individual’s complete state of health through the application of acquired knowledge, solving new problems using advanced technologies across various medical fields. They will collaborate with other healthcare professionals and master’s degree graduates in bioengineering, demonstrating the ability to interact and work effectively with medical colleagues, other healthcare professionals, and biomedical engineers.

**Program Structure and Educational Principles**  
The educational organization prioritizes the student within the learning process, personalizing timelines according to individual needs while emphasizing the relevance of proposed learning objectives aligned with the national core curriculum. Teaching methods include lectures, conferences, seminars, discussion groups, and journal clubs. All integrated courses are designed to ensure a unified and interdisciplinary approach to learning objectives.  

**Assessment Methods**  
For all integrated courses, certification assessments will be based on written and/or oral exams, as well as formative assessments conducted during the learning process.  

**Official Language of Instruction and Assessment**  
Italian  

**Professional Title**  
Medical Doctor (LM41)  

**Program Objective**  
This Medical and Surgery degree with a Biotechnology focus aims to train medical doctors with strong scientific knowledge, complemented by biotechnological, engineering, and digital expertise necessary for modern medical practice. Graduates will be equipped to integrate advanced technologies into clinical care, collaborate effectively in interdisciplinary teams, and continue evolving through lifelong learning. They will be prepared to address complex health challenges using innovative approaches rooted in biotechnology and engineering.  

**Key Features**  
- Integration of biotechnology and engineering principles into medical education.  
- Emphasis on digital health tools and data-driven decision-making.  
- Strong focus on ethical, legal, and social aspects of medical technology.  
- Preparation for collaboration with bioengineers and health technology specialists.  
- Commitment to continuous professional development through self-directed learning.  

This program ensures graduates are well-prepared to meet the demands of contemporary healthcare systems, leveraging interdisciplinary knowledge and technological innovation to improve patient outcomes and public health.

UNIVERSITY: Università degli Studi di Messina
COURSE: TECNICHE DI NEUROFISIOPATOLOGIA
SECTION: INFO STUDY PLANS
URL: https://unime.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10178

INFO STUDY PLANS
The course code is [3400]. It is a 3-year program leading to a degree in Neurophysiopathology Techniques. The program is structured according to the DM 270/2004 framework. The course is taught entirely in Italian. The program includes 180 CFU (Crediti Formativi Universitari).

Required knowledge for admission:
- Basic knowledge of human anatomy, physiology, and pathology
- Basic knowledge of neuroanatomy and neurophysiology
- Basic knowledge of medical ethics and law

Learning outcomes (Dublin descriptors):

I - Knowledge and understanding
• Acquire the foundations for qualitative and quantitative understanding of biological and physiological phenomena.
• Apply knowledge of neuroanatomy and neurophysiology, electroencephalography, and electronics to neurophysiological investigations.
• Deepen knowledge of neurological pathology and pediatric neuropsychiatry for application to neurophysiopathology techniques and functional exploration of the nervous system.
• Learn basic techniques and specific recording techniques applicable to acute patients, intensive care patients, and during surgical interventions.
• Learn the fundamentals of medical ethics, healthcare law, management, and legal and ethical aspects of the profession.
• Learn experimental electrophysiology techniques, neurosonology, and basic knowledge of neurorehabilitation and computerized signal acquisition and analysis.

These outcomes will be achieved through mandatory attendance at lectures, seminars, practical sessions, internships, and optional courses. Evaluation of knowledge and understanding will be conducted through exams, in-course assessments, and suitability tests for both theoretical courses and internships, as well as the final exam.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding
• Develop the professional skills specified in the profile.
• Correctly implement specific diagnostic methodologies (basic electroencephalography with activation; surface electromyography and collaboration in invasive EMG exams; somatosensory, auditory, and visual evoked potentials; sleep and autonomic nervous system polygraphy; collaboration in extra- and intracranial Doppler ultrasound examinations).
• Develop an instrumental diagnostic and neurophysiological research program in collaboration with the specialist physician.
• Prepare a technical report.
• Verify electrocerebral activity using instrumental diagnostic methods for clinical and/or legal purposes.
• Set up and control instrumentation and equipment.
• Implement preventive measures to promote safety for patients, operators, and work environments.
• Acquire IT skills useful for managing service information systems and for self-education.

Evaluation of these skills will be conducted through internship assessments, exams, and the final exam.

III - Making judgments
• Interact and collaborate actively with multidisciplinary teams.
• Demonstrate organizational and relational skills.
• Orient professional conduct according to ethical, deontological, legal, and professional responsibility principles.
• Acquire the method for independent study and continuous professional development.

Maturity of these skills will develop and be verified during internships, where interaction with diverse people, professional profiles, structures, and methodologies will facilitate the development of independent critical thinking. Equal importance will be given to active participation in lectures, exam preparation, and the final exam, as well as other moments of maturity and verification.

IV - Communication skills
• Acquire the ability to conduct bibliographic research and updates, critically read scientific articles (also through knowledge of an EU language beyond Italian enabling understanding of international literature and updates).
• Synthesize and report content acquired during the training path or from reading texts and scientific articles independently.
• Use correct and appropriate language when interacting with subjects of different ages, abilities, gender, and socio-cultural conditions.
• Involve and reassure users throughout all phases of diagnostic activity.
• Use appropriate technical terminology for different investigation methodologies.

All skills will be supported by IT knowledge acquired in specific courses. Verification will be conducted through exams, including internship exams, and the final exam.

V - Learning skills
• Develop interest in acquiring knowledge as a means to enrich professional skills.
• Develop motivation for continuous updating.
• Develop openness to integration and ability to extrapolate between technical knowledge and humanistic knowledge.
• Acquire awareness of available options for further studies and motivation to pursue them.

These skills will be developed and verified through exam preparation, internship attendance (where theory is combined with laboratory practice), and critical use of bibliographic resources for final exam preparation.

Classe di laurea L/SNT1 - Classe delle lauree in Professioni sanitarie, infermieristiche e professione sanitaria ostetrica Corso Interateneo No Accesso Programmato Sede MESSINA Altre sedi PRIOLO Dipartimento MEDICINA CLINICA E SPERIMENTALE Sito web https://infermieristica.cdl.unime.it  Requisiti di accesso Titoli obbligatori
[ TSS ]
Titolo di Scuola Superiore Ruoli Student mobility manager GIUSEPPINELLA MELITA Presidente CONCETTA CRISAFULLI Coordinatore CONCETTA CRISAFULLI Programma, testi e obiettivi Accesso ad ulteriori studi.
Il titolo dà accesso ai Corsi di Laurea Magistrale e a Corsi di Master Universitario di primo livello Status professionale conferito dal titolo.
Abilitante alla professione sanitaria di INFERMIERE Caratteristiche prova finale.
Per essere ammesso all'esame finale di laurea, lo studente deve aver superato tutti gli esami di profitto, ed avere avuto una valutazione positiva del tirocinio.
L’esame finale, con valore di Esame di Stato abilitante alla professione, è organizzato in due sessioni in periodi concordati su base nazionale.
L'esame finale – sostenuto dinanzi ad una Commissione nominata dalla competente Autorità accademica e composta a norma di legge - comprende: la discussione di un elaborato di natura teorico-applicativa; una prova di dimostrazione di abilità pratiche.
L'esame finale non può essere ripetuto più di una volta.
Conoscenze richieste per l'accesso.
a)Programmazione degli accessi Possono essere ammessi al Corso di Laurea in Infermieristica, candidati che siano in possesso di Diploma di Scuola Secondaria superiore o di titolo equipollente o di titolo conseguito all'estero riconosciuto idoneo ai sensi della normativa vigente e che siano qualificati in posizione utile all'esame di ammissione. L'eame di ammissione consiste in una prova con domande a risposta multipla su temi di: cultura generale, chimica, biologia, fisica, matematica e logica. Sono consentiti i passaggi da un Corso di Laurea all'altro di Area Sanitaria, senza ripetere il concorso di ammissione dietro rilascio di nulla osta da parte del Consiglio di Struttura Didattica. Il numero massimo degli studenti iscrivibili a ciascun Corso di Laurea è stabilito dalle competenti Autorità in relazione alle strutture ed al personale docente disponibile. Il numero programmato di accessi al primo anno di corso è definito ai sensi dell'art. 3, c.2 della Legge 264 del 2 settembre 1999 (Norme in materia di accesso ai corsi universitari).
b) Debito formativo L'organizzazione didattica del CL in Infermieristica prevede che gli studenti ammessi al I anno di corso possiedano una adeguata preparazione iniziale, conseguita negli studi precedentemente svolti.
Ciò premesso, tutti gli studenti che hanno superato l'esame di ammissione al I Anno del Corso di Laurea, rispondendo in modo corretto a meno della metà delle domande riguardanti i singoli argomenti di Fisica, Chimica e Biologia sono ammessi con un debito formativo, per una o più di una delle discipline in questione, che sono tenuti a sanare nel corso del I semestre/I anno. Allo scopo di consentire l'annullamento del debito formativo, il Consiglio di Corso istituisce attività didattiche propedeutiche che saranno svolte nell'arco del 1° semestre del primo anno di corso e che dovranno essere obbligatoriamente seguite dagli studenti in debito. Tali attività didattiche propedeutiche saranno garantite dai docenti del Corso di Laurea, sulla base di un ampliamento del loro impegno didattico e tutoriale. La verifica dei risultati conseguiti nelle attività didattiche propedeutiche avverrà al termine dei corsi di recupero.
Obiettivi formativi specifici.
I laureati nella classe sono dotati di un'adeguata preparazione nelle discipline di base, tale da consentire loro sia la migliore comprensione dei più rilevanti elementi, anche in relazione al genere, che sono alla base dei processi fisiologici e patologici ai quali è rivolto il loro intervento preventivo, terapeutico, palliativo e complementare, sia alla massima integrazione con le altre professioni.
Devono inoltre saper utilizzare almeno una lingua dell'Unione Europea, oltre l'italiano, nell'ambito specifico di competenza e per lo scambio di informazioni generali.
Titolo di studio rilasciato.
Laurea in INFERMIERISTICA Descrittori di Dublino: I - Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione I laureati di infermieristica devono conoscere e comprendere le
- scienze biomediche per la comprensione dei processi fisiologici e patologici connessi allo stato di salute e malattia delle persone nelle diverse età della vita;
- scienze psico sociali e umanistiche per la comprensione delle dinamiche relazionali normali e patologiche e delle reazioni di difesa o di adattamento delle persone a situazioni di disagio psichico, sociale e di sofferenza fisica;
- le teorie di apprendimento e del cambiamento per la comprensione dei processi educativi rivolti ai cittadini o ai pazienti;
- scienze infermieristiche generali e cliniche per la comprensione dei campi di intervento dell'infermieristica, del metodo clinico che guida un approccio efficace all'assistenza, delle tecniche operative di intervento e delle evidenze che guidano la presa di decisioni;
- scienze etiche, legali e sociologiche per la comprensione della complessità organizzativa del Sistema Sanitario, dell'importanza e dell'utilità di agire in conformità alla normativa e alle direttive nonché al rispetto dei valori e dei dilemmi etici che si presentano via via nella pratica quotidiana; sono finalizzate inoltre a favorire la comprensione dell'autonomia professionale, delle aree di integrazione e di interdipendenza con altri operatori del team di cura;
- scienze igienico-preventive per la comprensione dei determinanti di salute, dei fattori di rischio, delle strategie di prevenzione sia individuali che collettive e degli interventi volti a promuovere la sicurezza degli operatori sanitari e degli utenti;
- discipline informatiche e linguistiche con particolare approfondimento della lingua inglese per la comprensione della letteratura scientifica infermieristica sia cartacea che on line.
Metodologie ed attività formative, strumenti didattici per sviluppare i risultati attesi:
- Lezioni per introdurre l’argomento;
- Lettura guidata ed applicazione;
- Video, dimostrazione di immagini, schemi e materiali, grafici;
- Costruzione di mappe cognitive.
Strumenti di valutazione per accertare il conseguimento dei risultati attesi:
- Esami scritti e orali, prove di casi a tappe.
II - Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione I laureati di infermieristica devono dimostrare capacità applicare conoscenze e di comprendere nei seguenti ambiti:
- integrare le conoscenze le abilità e le attitudini dell'assistenza per erogare una cura infermieristica sicure, efficaci e basate sulle evidenze;
- utilizzare un corpo di conoscenze teoriche derivanti dal Nursing, dalle scienze biologiche comportamentali e sociali e da altre discipline per riconoscere i bisogni delle persone assistite nelle varie età e stadi di sviluppo nelle diverse fasi della vita;
- integrare le conoscenze infermieristiche teoriche e pratiche con le scienze biologiche , psicologiche , socio culturali e umanistiche utili per comprendere gli individui di tutte le età, gruppi e comunità;
- utilizzare modelli teorici e modelli di ruolo dell'interno del processo di assistenza per facilitare la crescita, lo sviluppo e l'adattamento nella promozione, mantenimento e recupero della salute dei cittadini;
- interpretare e applicare i risultati della ricerca alla pratica infermieristica e collegare i processi di ricerca allo sviluppo teorico della disciplina infermieristica;
- erogare un'assistenza infermieristica sicura e basata sulle evidenze per aggiungere i risultati di salute o uno stato di compenso dell'assistito;
- condurre una valutazione completa e sistematica dei bisogni di assistenza del singolo individuo;
- utilizzare tecniche di valutazione per raccogliere dati in modo accurato sui principali problemi di salute degli assistiti;
- analizzare e interpretare in modo accurato i dati raccolti mediante l'accertamento dell'assistito;
pianificare l'erogazione dell'assistenza infermieristica in collaborazione con gli utenti e con il team di cura interdisciplinare;
- valutare i progressi delle cure in collaborazione con il team interdisciplinare;
- facilitare lo sviluppo di un ambiente sicuro per l'assistito assicurando costante vigilanza infermieristica;
- gestire una varietà di attività che sono richieste per erogare l'assistenza infermieristica ai pazienti in diversi contesti di cura sia ospedalieri che territoriali e residenziali.
Metodologie e attività formative, strumenti didattici per sviluppare i risultati attesi:
- lezioni;
- esercitazioni con applicazione;
- video, dimostrazioni di immagini, schemi e materiali, grafici;
- costruzione di mappe cognitive;
- discussione di casi in sottogruppi con presentazioni in sessioni plenarie;
- tirocinio con esperienze supervisionate da tutor in diversi contesti e con una progressiva assunzione di autonomia e responsabilità.
Strumenti di valutazione per accertare il conseguimento dei risultati attesi:
- esami scritti e orali, prove di casi a tappe, project -work, report;
- feedback di valutazione durante il tirocinio (attraverso portfolio, schede di valutazione strutturate e report clinici sulla pratica professionale);
- esame strutturato oggettivo a stazioni.
III - Autonomia di giudizio I laureati di infermieristica devono dimostrare autonomia di giudizio attraverso le seguenti abilità:
- assumere decisioni assistenziali;
- decidere priorità su gruppi di pazienti;
- decidere gli interventi da attribuire al personale di supporto;
- attuare l'assistenza infermieristica personalizzando le scelte sulla base delle similitudini e differenze delle persone assistite rispetto a valori, etnia e pratiche socio culturali;
- decidere gli interventi assistenziali appropriati che tengono conto delle influenze legali, politiche, geografiche, economiche, etiche e sociali;
- valutare criticamente gli esiti delle decisioni assistenziali assunte sulla base degli outcomes del paziente e degli standard assistenziali;
- assumere la responsabilità e rispondere del proprio operato durante la pratica professionale in conformità al profilo, al codice deontologico e a standard etici e legali;
- assumere decisioni attraverso un approccio scientifico di risoluzione dei problemi del paziente;
- analizzare i problemi organizzativi e proporre soluzioni;
- decidere in situazioni a diversità di posizioni (conflitti o dilemmi).
Metodologie e attività formative, strumenti didattici per sviluppare i risultati attesi:
- lezioni;
- lettura guidata ed esercizi di applicazione;
- video, dimostrazioni di immagini, schemi e materiali, grafici;
- discussione di casi in sottogruppi con presentazioni in sessioni plenarie;
- tirocinio con esperienze super-visionate da tutor in diversi contesti e con una progressiva assunzione di autonomia e responsabilità;
- sessioni di debriefing per riflettere e rielaborare esperienze di pratica professionale.
Strumenti di valutazione per accertare il conseguimento dei risultati attesi:
- esami scritti e orali, prove di casi a tappe;
- feedback di valutazione durante il tirocinio (attraverso portfolio, schede di valutazione strutturate e report clinici sulla pratica professionale);
- esame strutturato oggettivo a stazioni.
IV - Abilità comunicative I laureati d'infermieristica devono sviluppare le seguenti abilità comunicative:
- utilizzare abilità di comunicazione appropriate (verbali, non verbali e scritte) con gli utenti di tutte le età e con le loro famiglie all'interno del processo assistenziale e/o con altri professionisti sanitari in forma appropriata verbale, non verbale e scritta:
- utilizzare modalità di comunicazione appropriate nel team multi professionale;
- utilizzare principi di insegnamento e apprendimento per interventi informativi o educativi specifici rivolti a singoli utenti, a famiglie e a gruppi, e altri professionisti (operatori di supporto, studenti infermieri, infermieri);
- sostenere e incoraggiare gli utenti verso scelte di salute, rinforzando abilità di coping, l'autostima e potenziando le risorse disponibili;
- gestire conflitti derivanti da posizioni diverse;
- facilitare il coordinamento dell'assistenza per raggiungere gli esiti di cura sanitari concordati;
- collaborare con il team di cura per concordare modalità operativi e realizzare l'applicazione e lo sviluppo di protocolli e linee guida.
Metodologie ed attività formative, strumenti didattici per sviluppare i risultati attesi:
- Lezioni;
- Video e analisi critica di filmati, simulazioni, narrazione, testimonianze;
- Discussione di casi e di situazioni relazionali paradigmatiche in sottogruppi con presentazioni in sessioni plenarie;
- Tirocinio con esperienze supervisionate da tutor in diversi contesti con sessioni di debriefing per riflettere e rielaborare esperienze relazionali con l’utenza e con l’equipe.
Strumenti di valutazione per accertare il conseguimento dei risultati attesi:
- Osservazione di frame di filmati o scritti, di dialoghi con griglie strutturate;
- Feedback di valutazione durante il tirocinio (attraverso portfolio, schede di valutazione strutturate e report clinici);
- Esame strutturato oggettivo con stazioni con simulazioni sulle competenze relazionali.
Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione.
ITALIANO V - Capacità di apprendimento I laureati di infermieristica devono sviluppare le seguenti capacità di autoapprendimento:
- sviluppare abilità di studio indipendente;
- dimostrare la capacità di coltivare i dubbi e tollerare le incertezze derivanti dallo studio e dall'attività pratica;
- sviluppare la capacità di porsi interrogativi sull'esercizio della propria attività, pertinenti nei tempi, nei luoghi e agli interlocutori;
- dimostrare la capacità di ricercare con continuità le opportunità di autoapprendimento;
- dimostrare capacità di autovalutazione delle proprie competenze e delineare i propri bisogni di sviluppo e apprendimento;
- dimostrare capacità di apprendimento collaborativo e di condivisione della conoscenza all'interno delle equipe di lavoro;
dimostrare capacità e autonomia nel cercare le informazioni necessarie per risolvere problemi o incertezze della pratica professionale, selezionando criticamente fonti secondarie e primarie di evidenze di ricerca.
Strumenti didattici, metodologie e attività formative per sviluppare i risultati attesi:
- apprendimento basato sui problemi (PBL);
- impiego di mappe cognitive;
- Utilizzo di contratti e piani di apprendimento al fine di responsabilizzare lo studente nella pianificazione del suo percorso di tirocinio e nell’autovalutazione;
- Laboratori di metodologia della ricerca bibliografica cartacea e online;
- Lettura guidata alla valutazione critica della letteratura scientifica e professionale sia in italiano sia in inglese.
Strumenti di valutazione per accertare il conseguimento dei risultati attesi:
- Project work, report sui mandati di ricerca specifica;
- Supervisione tutoriale sul percorso di tirocinio;
- Partecipazione attiva alle sessioni di lavoro e di debriefing;
- Puntualità e qualità della presentazione degli elaborati

Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

**Physiotherapy Degree Program: Key Learning Outcomes and Assessment**  
*Taught in Italian, 3-year program emphasizing clinical practice, evidence-based methods, and professional development.*

---

### **I. Application of Knowledge & Understanding**  
- **Focus**: Practical skills in clinical settings (simulated and real patient scenarios), integrating theoretical knowledge.  
- **Teaching Methods**: Classroom instruction, laboratory sessions, supervised clinical internships (*Tirocinio professionalizzante* with 1:1 tutor ratio).  
- **Assessment**:  
  - Year-end exams (graded out of 30).  
  - Practical tests, case studies, journal club participation, and written reports.  

---

### **II. Critical Thinking & Autonomy**  
- **Focus**: Autonomous decision-making using clinical reasoning, evidence-based practice (EBP), and ethical judgment.  
- **Teaching Methods**: Case discussions, rehabilitation planning (*Piano/Programma riabilitativo*), and reflective practice.  
- **Assessment**:  
  - Analysis of complex cases.  
  - *Core Values* evaluation by clinical tutors (assessing professionalism, ethics, and clinical judgment).  

---

### **III. Communication Skills**  
- **Focus**: Effective communication with patients, families, and interdisciplinary teams; accurate documentation (e.g., *cartella fisioterapica*).  
- **Teaching Methods**: Role-playing, patient interaction simulations, and collaborative team projects.  
- **Assessment**:  
  - Written reports on patient interactions.  
  - Oral presentations (e.g., case summaries, rehabilitation plans).  

---

### **IV. Language of Instruction**  
- **Focus**: All teaching, assessments, and materials delivered in **Italian**.  
- **Note**: International students must demonstrate proficiency in Italian for clinical practice.  

---

### **V. Lifelong Learning & Self-Assessment**  
- **Focus**: Continuous professional development, self-evaluation, and adaptation to evolving EBP standards.  
- **Teaching Methods**: Research projects, journal club critiques, and reflective portfolios.  
- **Assessment**:  
  - Self-assessment tools.  
  - Final year research project and comprehensive exam.  

---

### **Program Structure Highlights**  
- **Duration**: 3 years, with annual assessments (graded out of 30).  
- **Key Tools**: *Core Values* framework, EBP integration, and e-learning modules.  
- **Outcome**: Graduates are equipped for autonomous clinical practice, interdisciplinary collaboration, and evidence-based decision-making in physiotherapy.  

*Note: Emphasis on hands-on experience, ethical practice, and Italian-language proficiency ensures alignment with local healthcare standards and professional expectations.*

[2448] CLINICAL AND PREVENTIVE PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES AND TECHNIQUES Bachelor's Degree Program

### Summary of the "Scienze e Tecniche Psicologiche Cliniche e Preventive" Program (Italy)

#### **Degree Title**  
**Dottore in Scienze e Tecnicche Psicologiche Cliniche e Preventive**  
*(Clinical and Preventive Psychological Sciences Degree)*  

---

#### **Professional Qualification**  
- **Post-Graduation Role**: **Psicologo Junior** (Junior Psychologist), regulated by:  
  - *D.P.R. 5 giugno 2001, n. 328* (Art. 51, Capo X)  
  - *Legge 11 luglio 2003, n. 170* (Art. 3).  
- **Registration Requirement**: Must obtain **abilitazione** (license) and register with **Albo Professionale, Sezione B** (junior psychologists).  
- **Work Context**: Operates under supervision of a **full-licensed psychologist (Albo A)** in:  
  - Schools, social services, healthcare, rehabilitation, and community settings.  

---

#### **Key Competencies Acquired**  
1. **Assessment & Evaluation**:  
   - Use of psychological tools (interviews, observations, psychometrics) to assess mental and behavioral functioning across age groups and social contexts.  
2. **Preventive & Promotive Interventions**:  
   - Design and implement basic psychological interventions for:  
     - Preventing distress, promoting well-being, and strengthening resources (individual, family, groups, organizations).  
     - Supporting disability inclusion and social integration.  
3. **Analysis of Psychological Distress**:  
   - Identify and analyze psychological/behavioral disorders in diverse life stages and contexts.  
4. **Collaboration & Teamwork**:  
   - Work in multidisciplinary teams to support health, rehabilitation, and community well-being.  
5. **Research & Data Handling**:  
   - Collect, code, and statistically analyze psychological data for research purposes.  

---

#### **Professional Functions**  
- **Under Supervision of Albo A Psychologists**, graduates can:  
  - Conduct preliminary psychological assessments (e.g., interviews, psychometric tests).  
  - Participate in planning and evaluating psychological interventions (for individuals, families, groups, communities).  
  - Apply psychological tools for:  
    - School/work guidance, human resource management, and preventive education.  
    - Promoting health, preventing distress, and supporting disability.  
  - Deliver psychoeducational programs to foster personal growth and social participation.  

---

#### **Learning Outcomes (Based on Italian Framework)**  
| **Outcome**               | **Description**                                                                 |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Autonomy of Judgment**  | Critically analyze psychological phenomena using evidence-based approaches.      |
| **Communication Skills**  | Present findings orally/written using psychological terminology and scientific standards. |
| **Learning Capacity**     | Self-assess study methods and adapt to lifelong learning (e.g., continuing education). |
| **Professional Ethics**   | Apply ethical and deontological principles in all professional activities.      |

---

#### **Work Settings**  
- **Sectors**: Education (schools), healthcare (hospitals, clinics), social services, rehabilitation centers, community organizations.  
- **Collaboration**: With doctors, educators, social workers, and other professionals focused on prevention and well-being.  

---

#### **Key Legal References**  
- **D.P.R. 328/2001**: Defines the role of "Psicologo Junior" (Section B of the Albo).  
- **Law 170/2003**: Confirms the professional title and scope of practice.  

---

### **Why This Program?**  
This degree prepares students for **entry-level roles** in psychology, emphasizing **preventive care** and **community well-being**. Graduates gain practical skills for direct client work (under supervision) and contribute to multidisciplinary teams in public and private sectors.  

> 💡 **Note**: Full licensure (Albo A) requires additional exams and experience beyond this degree. The program is a **mandatory step** toward becoming a licensed psychologist in Italy.

[3011] MEDICINE AND SURGERY Master's Degree Single Cycle 6 years

-----

**Medical and Surgery Degree Program with a Biotechnology Focus (LM41)**

**I. Knowledge and Understanding**  
The program aims to train medical doctors with solid scientific knowledge, integrated with biotechnological and engineering expertise essential for practicing medicine in a technologically advanced society. Graduates will possess comprehensive knowledge of the human body, diseases, treatments, and preventive measures, including the biological, psychological, and social aspects of health and illness. They will understand the principles of biotechnology, engineering, and digital tools relevant to modern medical practice. This includes knowledge of molecular biology, genetics, bioinformatics, medical devices, and data analysis techniques. Graduates will also be familiar with ethical, legal, and social implications of biotechnology and digital health applications.

**II. Autonomy of Judgment**  
Graduates will be able to:  
1. Apply scientific knowledge to diagnose and treat patients, considering individual differences and social contexts.  
2. Evaluate and select appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic technologies, including digital tools and biotechnological innovations.  
3. Make informed decisions in complex clinical scenarios, balancing evidence-based medicine with patient preferences.  
4. Exercise professional responsibility in patient care and community health, adhering to medical ethics and deontological codes.  
5. Reflect critically on their professional practice, including interactions with patients and colleagues, methods used, and emotional experiences.  
6. Choose and implement suitable hardware and software technologies for patient care, respecting the social and human context of healthcare delivery.

**III. Communication Skills**  
Graduates will be able to:  
1. Listen attentively to understand and synthesize relevant information on health issues.  
2. Communicate clearly and effectively with patients and their families, enabling shared decision-making.  
3. Collaborate efficiently with colleagues, departments, communities, and media.  
4. Work effectively in interdisciplinary teams involving healthcare professionals.  
5. Demonstrate foundational teaching skills and appropriate attitudes toward others.  
6. Show cultural sensitivity to enhance interactions with patients and communities.  
7. Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.  
8. Maintain accurate and comprehensive medical documentation.  
9. Summarize and present information tailored to the audience’s needs, discussing achievable and acceptable action plans for individuals and communities.  
10. Communicate technical expertise with bioengineers, health technology designers, and bioinformaticians to identify optimal diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

**IV. Learning Ability**  
Graduates will develop the capacity for lifelong, self-directed learning, including:  
1. Collecting, organizing, and interpreting health and biomedical information from diverse resources and databases.  
2. Gathering specific patient information from clinical data management systems.  
3. Using information and communication technologies to support diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices, as well as health monitoring.  
4. Understanding the applications and limitations of information technology in healthcare.  
5. Maintaining a well-organized medical practice archive for analysis and improvement.

**V. Professional Competencies**  
**Role in the Work Context**  
Graduates will practice as medical doctors within the framework of European Community regulations, national and regional laws, both within the National Health Service (SSN) and in private or contracted facilities. Their primary objective is to maintain or restore each individual’s complete state of health through the application of acquired knowledge, solving new problems using advanced technologies across various medical fields. They will collaborate with other healthcare professionals and master’s degree graduates in bioengineering, demonstrating the ability to interact and work effectively with medical colleagues, other healthcare professionals, and biomedical engineers.

**Program Structure and Educational Principles**  
The educational organization prioritizes the student within the learning process, personalizing timelines according to individual needs while emphasizing the relevance of proposed learning objectives aligned with the national core curriculum. Teaching methods include lectures, conferences, seminars, discussion groups, and journal clubs. All integrated courses are designed to ensure a unified and interdisciplinary approach to learning objectives.  

**Assessment Methods**  
For all integrated courses, certification assessments will be based on written and/or oral exams, as well as formative assessments conducted during the learning process.  

**Official Language of Instruction and Assessment**  
Italian  

**Professional Title**  
Medical Doctor (LM41)  

**Program Objective**  
This Medical and Surgery degree with a Biotechnology focus aims to train medical doctors with strong scientific knowledge, complemented by biotechnological, engineering, and digital expertise necessary for modern medical practice. Graduates will be equipped to integrate advanced technologies into clinical care, collaborate effectively in interdisciplinary teams, and continue evolving through lifelong learning. They will be prepared to address complex health challenges using innovative approaches rooted in biotechnology and engineering.  

**Key Features**  
- Integration of biotechnology and engineering principles into medical education.  
- Emphasis on digital health tools and data-driven decision-making.  
- Strong focus on ethical, legal, and social aspects of medical technology.  
- Preparation for collaboration with bioengineers and health technology specialists.  
- Commitment to continuous professional development through self-directed learning.  

This program ensures graduates are well-prepared to meet the demands of contemporary healthcare systems, leveraging interdisciplinary knowledge and technological innovation to improve patient outcomes and public health.

COURSE: [2449] CLINICAL AND HEALTH PSYCHOLOGY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN (QUALIFYING FOR THE PSYCHOLOGIST PROFESSION)

**Summary: Bachelor's in Clinical and Health Psychology Across the Lifespan**  

This program prepares graduates to work in **clinical and health psychology**, emphasizing a **lifespan approach** (from childhood to old age) and **evidence-based practices**. Graduates develop competencies in:  
- **Autonomy of Judgment**: Critically assessing individual, family, and contextual factors; making ethical, evidence-driven decisions; and managing complex psychological challenges.  
- **Communication**: Effectively engaging with clients, interdisciplinary teams, and stakeholders through oral and written reports (e.g., psychological evaluations, intervention plans).  
- **Lifelong Learning**: Continuously updating skills via scientific literature, professional collaboration, and reflective practice.  
- **Professional Skills**: Conducting **multidimensional psychological diagnostics** (e.g., cognitive, emotional, relational), designing **preventive, therapeutic, and rehabilitative interventions**, and working in **multidisciplinary teams** (e.g., with medical professionals).  

**Professional Scope** (post-registration with the *Ordine degli Psicologi*):  
- Deliver **psychological support, prevention, and well-being promotion** across all life domains (social, professional, daily life) in **public/private institutions**.  
- Perform **psychodiagnostic assessments** focused on psychosocial distress.  
- Lead **multidisciplinary interventions** for individuals, couples, families, and communities.  
- Provide **consultation, expert opinions (peritia), supervision, training, and rehabilitation services**.  

**Key Requirements**:  
- Completion of a **practical evaluation internship (TPV)** and **final thesis** demonstrating applied skills.  
- **Ethical and deontological adherence** in all professional activities.  
- **Continuous professional development** to address evolving research and societal needs.  

This program equips graduates to address psychological challenges holistically, integrating **cultural, gender, and institutional contexts** while prioritizing **evidence-based outcomes** and **client-centered care**.

Mandatory titles [TSS]

L/SNT3
PROGRAMME
The programme provides the necessary knowledge and skills for the healthcare profession of Neurophysiology Technician, enabling the application of diagnostic techniques in neurophysiology and functional exploration of the nervous system.
LEARNING OUTCOMES
I - Knowledge and understanding
• Acquire the foundations for qualitative and quantitative understanding of biological and physiological phenomena.
• Apply knowledge of neuroanatomy and neurophysiology, electroencephalography, and electronics to neurophysiological investigations.
• Deepen knowledge of neurological pathology and pediatric neuropsychiatry for application in neurophysiology techniques and functional exploration of the nervous system.
• Learn basic techniques and specific recording techniques applicable to acute patients, intensive care patients, and during surgical interventions.
• Learn the fundamentals of medical ethics, healthcare law, management, and legal and ethical aspects of the profession.
• Learn experimental electrophysiology techniques, neurosonology, and basic knowledge of neurorehabilitation and acquisition and analysis of signals via computerized systems.
These outcomes will be achieved through mandatory attendance at lectures, seminars, practical exercises, internships, and optional courses. Evaluation of this knowledge and understanding capability will be conducted through exams, in-course assessments, and suitability tests for both theoretical courses and internships, as well as the final exam.
II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding
• Develop the professional skills specified in the profile.
• Correctly implement specific diagnostic methodologies (basic electroencephalography and with activations; surface electromyography and collaboration in invasive EMG exams; somatosensory, auditory, and visual evoked potentials; sleep and autonomic nervous system polygraphy; collaboration in extra- and intracranial Doppler ultrasound examinations).
• Develop a diagnostic instrumental and neurophysiological research program in collaboration with the specialist physician.
• Draft a technical report.
• Verify electrocerebral activity through diagnostic-instrumental methods for clinical and/or legal purposes.
• Prepare and control instrumentation and equipment.
• Implement preventive measures to promote safety for patients, operators, and work environments.
• Acquire IT skills useful for managing service information systems and personal self-education.
Evaluation of these skills will be conducted through internship assessments, exams, and the final exam.
III - Judgment autonomy
• Actively interact and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.
• Demonstrate organizational and relational skills.
• Orient professional conduct according to ethical, deontological, legal, and professional responsibility principles.
• Acquire the method for independent study and continuous professional development.
Maturity of these capabilities will be developed and verified during internships, where interaction with diverse people, professional profiles, structures, and methodologies will facilitate the development of independent critical thinking. Equal importance will be given to active participation in lectures, exam preparation, and the final exam, as well as other moments of maturation and verification.
IV - Communication skills
• Acquire the ability to conduct bibliographic research and updates, critically read scientific articles (also through knowledge of an EU language beyond Italian, enabling comprehension of international literature and updates).
• Synthesize and report content acquired during the training path or from reading texts and scientific articles independently.
• Use correct and appropriate language when interacting with subjects of different ages, abilities, gender, and socio-cultural conditions.
• Involve and reassure users throughout all phases of diagnostic activity.
• Use appropriate technical terms for different investigation methodologies.
All skills will be supported by IT knowledge acquired in specific courses. Verification will be conducted through exams, including internship exams, and the final exam.
V - Learning ability
• Develop interest in acquiring knowledge as a means to enrich professional skills.
• Develop motivation for continuous updating.
• Develop openness to integration and ability to extrapolate between technical knowledge and humanistic knowledge.
• Acquire awareness of available options for further studies and motivation to pursue them.
This ability will be developed and verified through exam preparation, internship attendance (where theory is combined with laboratory practice), and critical use of bibliographic resources for final exam preparation.

Titolo di Scuola Superiore Ruoli Student mobility manager GIUSEPPINELLA MELITA Presidente CONCETTA CRISAFULLI Coordinatore CONCETTA CRISAFULLI Programma, testi e obiettivi Accesso ad ulteriori studi.
