Obiettivi formativi specifici.
I principali obiettivi formativi del CdS sono i seguenti:
- l'acquisizione di competenze linguistico-culturali integrate, tali da consentire ai discenti di muoversi agevolmente negli ambiti professionali cui la laurea dà accesso;
- costituisce inoltre obiettivo formativo specifico l'acquisizione di competenze linguistiche spendibili in diversi settori: nell'ambito delle attività di mediazione, a fronte del fenomeno in costante crescita dell'intermediazione in contesti multilinguistici e multietnici; in direzione dello sviluppo di un'offerta qualificata nei settori in cui la competenza linguistica svolge un ruolo veicolare nei processi di trasferimento di dati e informazioni (industria elettronica e informatica, imprese chimico-farmaceutiche, rete di servizi a supporto del 'transhipment' e altri modelli avanzati di relazioni commerciali); in direzione delle attività di assistenza linguistica alle imprese e agli enti e istituti pubblici;
- l’acquisizione di competenze linguistiche e metalinguistiche finalizzate alla redazione, in lingua, e alla traduzione di testi sia pratici che letterari.
Gli obiettivi formativi verranno raggiunti attraverso un percorso di studio comprendente discipline strettamente connesse con la competenza tecnica delle diverse lingue, accompagnate dallo studio delle discipline dei seguenti settori: 1) filologico, relativo allo studio delle fasi antiche e/o medievali delle lingue oggetto di studio; 2) linguistico, relativo all’analisi delle principali strutture in cui sono organizzate le lingue e ai i principali metodi impiegati per classificare le lingue del mondo; 3) linguistico-traduttivo, relativo alle teorie alla base delle scelte traduttive e interpretative di un testo; 4) letterario, relativo allo studio della letteratura italiana e alla storia delle letterature delle lingue di studio; 5) sociologico, relativo alla conoscenza delle dinamiche sociali connesse ai processi culturali e comunicativi; 6) storico, relativo alle storie sia generali che specialistiche, finalizzato all’apprendimento della distinzione tra lo svolgersi fattuale degli eventi e gli approcci interpretativi che li riguardano, oltre che all’analisi delle fonti che influenzano l’esito del lavoro storiografico; 7) geografico, relativo all’analisi dei principali aspetti ambientali, paesaggistici, demografici ed economici del territorio.
Titolo di studio rilasciato.
Laurea in LINGUE , LETTERATURE STRANIERE E TECNICHE DELLA MEDIAZIONE LINGUISTICA Descrittori di Dublino: I - Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione I laureati delle classi L11 ed L12 devono possedere una piena conoscenza della struttura, delle funzioni, sociali e pragmatiche, e della storia delle due lingue straniere scelte (Lingua A e Lingua B), a cui fa da sfondo una ricca serie di discipline di inquadramento, classificabili in tre diverse aree: quella linguistico-traduttiva; quella filologico-letteraria e quella geo-storica e sociologica.
La preparazione verrà verificata attraverso esami sia scritti che orali, dando ampio spazio ad attività di valutazione che riflettano le attività professionali di pertinenza del corso di laurea, ossia analisi metalinguistiche sui meccanismi di produzione e interpretazione della comunicazione di micro e macro-livello e analisi testuali interpretative e critiche; simulazioni di contesto professionale, quali attività pratica di interpretazione di trattativa e svolgimento di traduzioni.
II - Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione In considerazione della globalizzazione quale sfida apicale della contemporaneità, il percorso di 'Lingue e culture' permetterà al laureato, oltre a esprimersi con fluidità nelle due lingue straniere scelte, di utilizzarle con cognizione metalinguistica, associandole in modo appropriato ai relativi contesti socioculturali, multilinguistici e multiculturali, e adottando strategie e soluzioni adeguate alle svariate situazioni comunicative. Le competenze linguistiche avanzate, associate agli strumenti forniti dall'area delle scienze filologico-letterarie attraverso l'analisi sia letterario-culturale sia filologico-linguistica dei testi, rendono il laureato della classe L11 capace di interpretare linguaggi specifici legati a fenomeni letterari o culturali connessi con le lingue di studio, sia in prospettiva sincronica che diacronica. I laureati che avranno crediti in numero sufficiente in opportuni gruppi di settori potranno, come previsto dalla legislazione vigente, partecipare alle prove di ammissione per i percorsi di formazione per l’insegnamento secondario.
Il percorso di 'Mediazione linguistica' consentirà al laureato di applicare le competenze acquisite per gestire in modo professionale i processi di interpretazione e traduzione di testi di diversa tipologia, incluso settoriali, in italiano e nelle lingue straniere di studio. Si avvarrà di strumenti e metodologie dell’analisi linguistica, traduttologica e lessicografica combinando le conoscenze interdisciplinari, individuando i problemi e proponendo le soluzioni adeguate in funzione dei destinatari. Le abilità informatiche assimilate gli permetteranno di utilizzare gli strumenti multimediali allo scopo di valorizzare, come fine ultimo, la mediazione interculturale.
Le tipologie di attività formative attraverso cui i risultati saranno conseguiti e verificati sono: 1. gli ambiti disciplinari presenti nella tabella delle attività formative, relativamente alle seguenti aree: linguistico-traduttiva; filologico-letteraria; area geo-storica e sociologica; 2. il tirocinio formativo e di orientamento, presso aziende o enti di ricerca, finalizzato a porre lo studente in contatto con le realtà lavorative più adeguate alla sua preparazione ed al suo arricchimento professionale; 3. le attività seminariali organizzate dai singoli docenti o comunque interne all'Ateneo; 4. I laboratori linguistici legati alle discipline di interpretariato e traduzione. Rientrano inoltre nelle tipologie formative necessarie per conseguire e verificare i risultati del CdS: 1. gli esami di profitto, orali e scritti; 2. una prova finale, necessaria per il conseguimento della laurea, consistente nella discussione pubblica dell’elaborato dalla quale la Commissione esaminatrice possa accertare la maturità culturale e la capacità di elaborazione del candidato, nonché la qualità del lavoro svolto.
III - Autonomia di giudizio I laureati di entrambe le classi dovranno acquisire la capacità di analizzare testi, orali e scritti, nel contesto appropriato. Dovranno essere in grado di individuare e riconoscere le variabili diastratiche e diafasiche in cui si situano gli atti linguistici, mostrando di saperli collocare negli appropriati contesti storici, sociali e politici.
Tali capacità critiche sono acquisite attraverso attività formative seminariali, confronti interdisciplinari e tirocini e sono verificate con prove in itinere ed esami scritti ed orali.
IV - Abilità comunicative Le abilità comunicative costituiscono il fulcro del percorso di studi dell'interclasse. Tutte le attività del corso di laurea - al di là del contenuto specifico delle singole discipline - adottano metodologie rivolte alla costruzione delle abilità comunicative, il conseguimento delle quali viene verificato sistematicamente attraverso prove scritte e orali, che possono prevedere anche colloqui in intinere.
Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione.
ITALIANO V - Capacità di apprendimento La finalizzazione del corso di studio è principalmente mirata a formare laureati pronti ad intraprendere percorsi di studio magistrali nei quali essi amplieranno, approfondiranno e completeranno le conoscenze e competenze già acquisite.
Il consolidamento delle capacità di apprendimento, anche con l'ausilio di servizi di tutorato, procede di pari passo con le verifiche continue, semestrali e annuali, che consentono di seguire gli studenti lungo l'intero percorso di studi, rendendoli idonei al proseguimento della loro attività formativa.
Competenze associate alla funzione.
mediatore linguistico e culturale Uso e manipolazione dei codici linguistici appropriati nella comunicazione ordinaria e specialistica.
Esperto della traduzione e dei servizi di mediazione Competenze linguistiche e metalinguistiche finalizzate alla redazione, in lingua, e alla traduzione di testi sia pratici che letterari. Abilità di lettura, comprensione ed espressione scritta e orale nelle lingue prescelte; conoscenza avanzata degli usi pragmatici della lingua. Uso e manipolazione dei codici linguistici ai fini dell'attivazione del circuito della comunicazione ordinaria e specialistica.
Funzione in contesto di lavoro.
mediatore linguistico e culturale Operare nell'ambito della produzione e dei servizi di mediazione interlinguistica.
Esperto della traduzione e dei servizi di mediazione Tradurre e interpretare testi in lingua straniera; interagire in contesti multiculturali; identificare e trasmettere contenuti specialistici e settoriali.

COURSE TITLE: Letters
COURSE DESCRIPTION: The Letters programme provides a comprehensive education in literary, linguistic, and cultural studies, preparing students for professional roles in cultural services, editorial activities, and education. - Methodological training: Critical analysis, research techniques
- Practical components: Seminars, workshops, internships

- Degree: Bachelor's degree (Laurea triennale)

- Literary analysis: Classical, medieval, modern, and contemporary literature
- Linguistic studies: Historical linguistics, sociolinguistics
- Cultural studies: Heritage management, cultural policy
- Methodology: Critical reading, research techniques

LEARNING OUTCOMES (DUBLIN DESCRIPTORS):

I - Knowledge and Understanding
- Demonstrates comprehensive knowledge of literary, linguistic, and cultural phenomena
- Understands historical contexts of literary works

II - Application of Knowledge and Understanding
- Analyzes complex texts critically
- Develops informative and divulgative texts
- Uses basic IT tools, internet search engines, and word processing software
- Designs and organizes cultural products and services

III - Judgment Skills
- Independently navigates topics within their study area
- Organizes complex documentary information logically
- Interprets literary, linguistic, historical, and artistic phenomena autonomously
- Applies analytical methods to ancient, modern, and contemporary civilizations
- Works effectively in teams

IV - Communication Skills
- Expresses humanistic research results with precision
- Collaborates in group work on linguistic, literary, archaeological, and historical topics
- Communicates effectively in both specialized and non-specialized contexts

V - Learning Skills
- Critically analyzes information and develops effective learning methods
- Establishes interdisciplinary connections
- Conducts bibliographic research proficiently
- Continuously updates knowledge with methodological awareness

- Collaborates with specialists in cataloging and library management
- Organizes exhibition projects and educational activities
- Maintains public relations and user consultations

Collaborator in Editorial and Editorial Activities:
- Edits and revises texts in public administration
- Creates editorial content for cultural information
- Collaborates with editorial specialists
- Manages research, data, and document archiving

[4035] PHILOSOPHY Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

**Program Overview**  
This Philosophy degree program in Italy integrates theoretical knowledge of Western philosophy, cultural history, and critical analysis with practical skills for professional application. Designed to prepare graduates for roles in cultural industries, communication, education, and personnel management, the curriculum emphasizes critical thinking, communication, and interdisciplinary problem-solving. All instruction and assessment are conducted in **Italian**.

---

### **Learning Outcomes (Based on Dublin Descriptors)**  
**I. Knowledge and Understanding**  
- Mastery of Western cultural history, philosophical traditions, and historical evolution of contemporary issues.  
- Ability to analyze complex social, cultural, and historical phenomena using philosophical and hermeneutic tools.  
- Proficiency in bibliographic and archival research methods across disciplines.  

**II. Application of Knowledge**  
- Critical analysis of contemporary societal challenges through historical and philosophical lenses.  
- Development of argumentative strategies to clarify problems and propose solutions.  
- Adaptation of philosophical methodologies to diverse professional contexts (e.g., cultural projects, personnel management).  

**III. Autonomy of Judgment**  
- Formation of independent, value-based judgments on cultural products and socio-historical contexts.  
- Practice of dialectical reasoning through debates on philosophical texts and modern issues.  

**IV. Communication Skills**  
- Effective oral and written communication tailored to public, media, and professional audiences.  
- Ability to distinguish and apply different communication languages (e.g., journalistic, academic, multimedia).  

**V. Learning Ability**  
- Development of critical research methodologies to synthesize information and foster conceptual creativity.  
- Use of digital tools (e-learning, group projects) to enhance reflective thinking and linguistic precision.  

---

### **Teaching Methods**  
- **Lectures** for theoretical foundations.  
- **Seminars and group exercises** for critical analysis and debate.  
- **Practical workshops** on writing, media communication, and project management.  
- **Thesis development** and oral defense for final assessment.  

---

### **Key Competencies for Professional Roles**  
#### **1. Cultural Industry & Communication Sector**  
- **Core Skills**:  
  - Mastery of Italian language and concise, persuasive writing.  
  - Ability to filter, organize, and present information (e.g., for media, events, or editorial projects).  
  - Project coordination (e.g., cultural events, multimedia content creation).  
  - Editing, interview design, and external communication.  
- **Example Roles**:  
  - Ideating and managing cultural events or media campaigns.  
  - Editing texts for print/digital platforms.  
  - Coordinating teams for project execution.  

#### **2. Education, Orientation & Personnel Management**  
- **Core Skills**:  
  - Interpersonal communication and group facilitation.  
  - Designing training programs and career orientation paths.  
  - Cultural mediation and social integration strategies.  
  - Applying socio-psychopedagogical methods to personnel management.  
- **Example Roles**:  
  - Managing employee recruitment and development in public/private organizations.  
  - Designing multicultural training programs for social integration.  
  - Supporting career guidance for students or professionals.  

---

### **Career Pathways**  
| **Sector**                          | **Key Responsibilities**                                                                 |
|-------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Cultural Industry & Communication** | - Planning cultural initiatives and media strategies.<br>- Editing content for print/digital media.<br>- Coordinating teams for event execution. |
| **Education & Personnel Management**  | - Organizing training programs for staff.<br>- Facilitating career orientation for students/workers.<br>- Mediating cultural/social integration in teams. |

---

### **Program Differentiators**  
- **Philosophy + Practical Skills**: Bridges abstract philosophical inquiry with real-world applications (e.g., critical analysis for media, cultural mediation for HR).  
- **Interdisciplinary Focus**: Integrates history, communication, and social sciences to address modern challenges.  
- **Career-Ready Curriculum**: Explicitly aligns competencies with job market demands in Italy’s cultural and educational sectors.  

This program equips graduates to thrive in dynamic fields requiring both deep intellectual rigor and adaptable professional skills. Graduates are prepared to contribute to cultural innovation, educational advancement, and strategic personnel development.

COURSE: [4072] ARCHAEOLOGICAL HERITAGE: TERRITORY, SETTLEMENTS, MATERIAL CULTURE
SECTION: General Description
URL: https://unime.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10523?annoOrdinamento=2021

[4072] ARCHAEOLOGICAL HERITAGE: TERRITORY, SETTLEMENTS, MATERIAL CULTURE Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

### **Archaeology Bachelor's Program: Key Overview**  
**Duration**: 3 years (Laurea Triennale)  
**Language of Instruction**: Italian (with mandatory English proficiency for professional communication).  
**Certification Requirement**: English language certification (e.g., B2 level or higher) for international collaboration and documentation.  

---

### **Core Learning Outcomes**  
1. **Knowledge & Understanding**  
   - Mastery of archaeological methods, historical context, and documentation (e.g., excavation diaries, ICCD cataloging).  
   - Critical analysis of archaeological sites, artifacts, and cultural heritage policies.  

2. **Practical Application**  
   - Conduct fieldwork (excavations, topographic surveys) under supervision.  
   - Classify artifacts, create technical reports, and support museum exhibitions.  
   - Use digital tools for research, data management, and multimedia communication.  

3. **Critical Thinking**  
   - Evaluate diverse methodologies and historical interpretations.  
   - Synthesize interdisciplinary data (e.g., archaeology, history, conservation) for context-specific solutions.  

4. **Communication**  
   - Write technical documents (e.g., excavation reports, museum labels) in Italian and English.  
   - Adapt communication for experts (e.g., academic papers) and public audiences (e.g., guided tours, educational content).  

5. **Lifelong Learning**  
   - Independently update knowledge via digital databases, academic literature, and field research.  
   - Prepare for advanced studies (e.g., master’s programs) or specialized roles.  

---

### **Key Competencies Developed**  
- **Fieldwork**: Excavation, topographic surveys, artifact documentation (US/UT sheets, ICCD catalogs).  
- **Technical Skills**: Manual/instrumental monument surveys, numismatic analysis, museum display design.  
- **Digital Literacy**: Use of databases, GIS, and multimedia tools for research and public engagement.  
- **Professional Ethics**: Adherence to MIBACT (Italian Ministry of Cultural Heritage) standards.  

---

### **Career Paths & Required Skills**  
| **Role**                          | **Key Responsibilities**                                                                 | **Program Alignment**                                                                 |
|-----------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Archaeological Collaborator**<br>(Archeologo III Fascia, MIBACT DM 244/2019) | Conduct excavations/surveys, document findings, prepare technical reports.             | Fieldwork labs, excavation practice, ICCD cataloging training.                      |
| **Museum Technician**             | Classify artifacts, design exhibitions, write educational materials (labels, panels). | Museum workshops, exhibition design courses, technical writing.                      |
| **Numismatic Specialist**         | Identify/categorize coins, assess authenticity, assign commercial value.               | Numismatics seminars, artifact analysis labs.                                       |
| **Cultural Heritage Guide**       | Lead educational tours, design tourist itineraries, explain sites to public audiences. | Public communication courses, guided tour simulations, multimedia presentation training. |

---

### **Assessment Methods**  
- **Theoretical**: Exams, in-term quizzes, final thesis (elaborato finale).  
- **Practical**: Lab reports, fieldwork diaries, internship evaluations, museum exhibition projects.  
- **Communication**: Final thesis defense, multimedia presentations, technical writing samples.  

---

### **Why This Program Stands Out**  
- **Hands-on Focus**: 30%+ of curriculum dedicated to fieldwork, labs, and internships (e.g., archaeological sites, museums).  
- **Industry Alignment**: Directly prepares students for MIBACT-certified roles (e.g., Archeologo III Fascia).  
- **Global Readiness**: English certification ensures competitiveness in international heritage projects.  

*Note: Graduates are equipped to work in public institutions (museums, heritage agencies), private firms, or as independent consultants in cultural tourism and conservation.*

[1287R] QUANTITATIVE METHODS FOR ECONOMICS AND FINANCE Master's Degree Program English Italian

-----

### Master's Program in **Quantitative Methods for Economics and Finance**  
*Two Specializations: Economics & Finance*  

---

#### **Program Overview**  
This Master’s program equips students with advanced quantitative skills to analyze economic and financial systems, combining theoretical knowledge with practical applications. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in public, private, and international contexts.  

---

#### **Specialization 1: Expert in Quantitative Economics**  
**Core Competencies:**  
- Advanced economic theory, macroeconomic analysis, and policy evaluation.  
- Statistical/mathematical tools for economic data analysis (e.g., forecasting, policy impact assessment).  
- Risk management and sustainability in economic systems.  
- Financial management of enterprises and public institutions.  
- Use of datasets for empirical economic research.  

**Key Job Roles:**  
- **Quantitative Economist** (e.g., analyzing market trends, fiscal policy impacts).  
- **Public Economic Officer** (e.g., designing economic strategies for government agencies).  
- **Economic Consultant** (e.g., advising businesses on market dynamics).  

**Typical Tasks:**  
- Conduct quantitative analysis of economic systems.  
- Evaluate direct/indirect impacts of corporate/public policies.  
- Link observed economic trends to theoretical models.  
- Support decision-making using econometric models.  

---

#### **Specialization 2: Expert in Quantitative Finance**  
**Core Competencies:**  
- Financial theory, portfolio management, and risk modeling.  
- Advanced statistical/mathematical tools for financial data (e.g., risk assessment, predictive analytics).  
- Financial regulations and market dynamics.  
- Management of financial datasets and scenario planning.  

**Key Job Roles:**  
- **Financial Analyst** (e.g., market analysis, investment strategies).  
- **Portfolio Manager** (e.g., optimizing asset allocation).  
- **Risk Manager** (e.g., assessing financial risks using quantitative models).  
- **Financial Consultant/Broker** (e.g., advising on complex financial products).  

**Typical Tasks:**  
- Apply quantitative tools to financial data for empirical analysis.  
- Develop predictive models for financial scenarios.  
- Design innovative tools for descriptive/predictive financial analysis.  
- Evaluate financial risks using statistical models.  

---

#### **Shared Program Features**  
- **Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors):**  
  - **Critical Analysis:** Independently assess economic/financial systems.  
  - **Communication:** Present findings in technical reports (English/Italian).  
  - **Autonomy:** Solve real-world problems using interdisciplinary knowledge.  
  - **Language:** **Italian** (primary instruction) and **English** (for technical materials and global collaboration).  

- **Practical Focus:**  
  - Case studies, data analysis (using real datasets), and group projects.  
  - Emphasis on **sustainability** (Economics track) and **financial innovation** (Finance track).  

---

#### **Career Pathways**  
| **Specialization**       | **Workplace Context**                          | **Global Relevance** |  
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------|  
| **Quantitative Economics** | Public institutions, international agencies (e.g., IMF), consulting firms. | High (policy-focused roles). |  
| **Quantitative Finance**   | Banks, asset management firms, fintech startups. | High (finance-driven roles). |  

---

#### **Why Choose This Program?**  
- **Dual Expertise:** Bridges economics *and* finance with advanced quantitative rigor.  
- **Industry Alignment:** Directly addresses demand for data-driven decision-making in both sectors.  
- **Global Readiness:** English proficiency ensures competitiveness in international markets.  

*Graduates are equipped to lead in complex economic/financial landscapes, leveraging data to shape strategy and policy.*

-----

The **Master's Program in Business Consulting and Management** (Consulenza e Gestione di Impresa) is designed to equip students with advanced competencies for high-level roles in business consulting and corporate management, aligned with the **Dublin Descriptors** of the European Higher Education Area. Below is a concise overview of its key features:

---

### **Core Focus Areas**  
1. **Knowledge & Expertise**  
   - Mastery of **financial accounting (IAS/IFRS)**, strategic planning, risk management, social accounting, and crisis management (e.g., restructuring, bankruptcy).  
   - Proficiency in **business planning**, financial control, and integrated management systems.  
   - Understanding of **legal and fiscal frameworks** for corporate operations.  

2. **Professional Skills**  
   - Solving complex business challenges (e.g., corporate restructuring, financial risk assessment).  
   - Preparing **business plans** for new ventures or existing enterprises.  
   - Applying **technology-driven communication** tools for data presentation.  

3. **Communication & Collaboration**  
   - Ability to convey technical insights clearly to **experts and non-experts**.  
   - Working effectively in **international teams** (taught in **Italian and English**).  
   - Strong written/oral communication for professional reporting and presentations.  

4. **Lifelong Learning**  
   - Continuous updating on industry trends, regulatory changes, and digital tools.  
   - Preparation for **advanced studies** (e.g., PhD) or independent research.  

---

### **Career Paths**  
Graduates qualify for **two primary professional roles**:  

#### **1. High-Level Business Consultant**  
- **Certifications**: Eligible for **Dottore Commercialista** (Chartered Accountant) and **Esperto Contabile** (with State Exam, *fascia A*).  
- **Roles**:  
  - Corporate advisor for **extraordinary operations** (mergers, acquisitions, valuations).  
  - Expert in **financial reporting (IAS/IFRS)**, legal audits, and crisis management (e.g., bankruptcy, restructuring).  
  - Specialist in **social accounting** and **risk control**.  

#### **2. Functional Manager**  
- **Roles in large enterprises**:  
  - **Chief Financial Officer (CFO)**, **Risk Manager**, **Internal Control Director**.  
  - **Strategic roles**: Head of Planning & Control, General Manager, or Operational Analyst.  
  - **Public/private sector**: Leading corporate functions in multinational firms or public institutions.  

---

### **Program Highlights**  
- **Language**: Taught in **Italian and English**; international internships/study abroad opportunities.  
- **Prerequisites**: Builds on **bachelor’s-level business/economics knowledge** (e.g., accounting, management).  
- **Professional Integration**: Prepares students for **Italian professional registers** (*albo*) and global business standards.  
- **Final Assessment**: Includes a **thesis defense** evaluating analytical, research, and communication skills.  

---

### **Why This Program?**  
- **Unique Value**: Bridges **technical accounting expertise** with **strategic management** for leadership roles.  
- **Industry Demand**: Addresses needs in **financial consulting**, **corporate governance**, and **digital transformation**.  
- **Global Relevance**: Aligns with international standards (e.g., IAS/IFRS) for cross-border career mobility.  

This program is ideal for students aiming to **lead in corporate finance, consulting, or strategic management** within dynamic business environments.

### **Summary of the *Management d'Impresa* (Business Management) Degree Program**  
*(Italian Higher Education, Class L-18)*  

#### **Program Overview**  
This interdisciplinary program combines **business management, economics, law, and quantitative methods** to prepare students for dynamic roles in corporate, public, and non-profit sectors. Taught in **Italian and English**, it emphasizes practical skills through case studies, internships (*tirocinio*), and project-based learning.  

---

#### **Key Learning Outcomes**  
1. **Knowledge & Skills**  
   - Strategic management, marketing, financial control, quality management, supply chain operations.  
   - Economic analysis, legal frameworks, and data-driven decision-making.  
   - Ability to design and interpret business models (*e.g., for startups or corporate strategy*).  

2. **Communication & Collaboration**  
   - Fluent communication in Italian/English for presentations, reports, and team collaboration.  
   - Cross-cultural competence for international work environments.  

3. **Autonomy & Critical Thinking**  
   - Analyze complex business scenarios and propose innovative solutions.  
   - Develop independent research and problem-solving skills for advanced studies or professional growth.  

4. **Professional Readiness**  
   - Access to **Chartered Accountant (Dottore Commercialista)** exams (after passing the state exam) and **agro-technical certification**.  
   - Prepares for roles requiring regulatory compliance (e.g., financial audits, strategic consulting).  

---

#### **Career Opportunities**  
Graduates are equipped for **mid-to-senior roles** across sectors:  
- **Managerial Positions**:  
  - Operations, finance, marketing, and supply chain management in SMEs or large corporations.  
  - Leadership roles in small businesses (e.g., *direttore generale*) or mid-level management in complex organizations.  
- **Consulting**:  
  - Strategic, financial, or quality management consulting (*e.g., for corporate clients or public institutions*).  
- **Administrative Roles**:  
  - Economic, administrative, or operational support in **private, public, or non-profit sectors** (e.g., government agencies, NGOs, multinational firms).  

---

#### **Unique Value Proposition**  
- **Interdisciplinary Edge**: Blends business acumen with economics, law, and data analytics.  
- **Global Relevance**: English proficiency and international case studies prepare students for global markets.  
- **Regulatory Access**: Direct pathway to professional certifications (e.g., *Dottore Commercialista*), enhancing career mobility in Italy.  

---

**Ideal For**: Students seeking a **versatile, practice-oriented business degree** with strong career pathways in management, consulting, and cross-sector leadership. The program bridges academic rigor with real-world application, emphasizing adaptability in evolving business landscapes.

### Summary of the Three-Year Degree in Business Economics (Economia Aziendale)  
**Program Overview**  
This three-year undergraduate program (Laurea Triennale) in Business Economics equips students with interdisciplinary skills in **economic, legal, and quantitative analysis**, preparing them for roles in accounting, management, and financial decision-making. The curriculum combines theoretical knowledge with practical training through case studies, internships, and project work. All instruction and assessments are conducted in **Italian**.  

---

### **Core Competencies Developed**  
1. **Autonomy of Judgment**  
   - Ability to analyze economic, social, and business data using quantitative methods.  
   - Form independent opinions through critical reflection on complex business scenarios.  
   - *Verification*: Evaluated during internships and final thesis preparation.  

2. **Communication Skills**  
   - Clearly convey complex ideas to diverse audiences (e.g., clients, teams).  
   - Master active listening, cross-cultural collaboration, and professional English (basic proficiency required).  
   - *Verification*: Oral presentations, group projects, and final thesis defense.  

3. **Learning Ability**  
   - Develop self-directed learning habits for continuous professional growth (e.g., lifelong learning, research).  
   - *Verification*: Independent study, data analysis tasks, and final thesis.  

4. **Professional Expertise**  
   - Mastery of accounting, tax, financial analysis, and management systems.  
   - *Verification*: Practical exercises, internships, and case studies.  

---

### **Professional Career Paths**  
Graduates are prepared for **entry-level roles** in private, public, and non-profit organizations, with potential for advancement after field experience. Key roles include:  

#### **1. Accountant/Consultant (Esperto Contabile)**  
   - **Responsibilities**: Handle accounting, tax compliance, financial reporting, and strategic planning.  
   - **Professional Path**: Qualifies for **Category B of the "Esperto Contabile" register** (requires internship + state exam).  
   - **Skills**: General accounting, legal frameworks, tax systems.  

#### **2. Managerial Roles**  
   - **Administration & Accounting Manager**: Oversee financial operations in SMEs (after initial field experience).  
   - **Planning & Control Manager**: Lead strategic planning, budgeting, and performance analysis.  
   - **Finance Manager**: Analyze financial data, manage investments, and support decision-making.  
   - **Skills**: Data-driven decision-making, cross-departmental collaboration.  

#### **3. Administrative & Support Roles**  
   - **Work Context**: SMEs, public institutions, non-profits.  
   - **Responsibilities**: Manage day-to-day operations, financial documentation, and reporting.  
   - **Skills**: Organizational efficiency, communication, basic financial literacy.  

---

### **Key Notes**  
- **Language**: All coursework and assessments are in Italian.  
- **Professional Requirements**: To become a certified **Esperto Contabile**, graduates must complete an internship and pass a state exam (beyond the degree).  
- **Career Trajectory**: The degree provides foundational skills for immediate entry into the workforce, with opportunities for specialization (e.g., finance, tax consulting) after gaining experience.  

This program bridges academic rigor with real-world application, positioning graduates for dynamic careers in business and finance across Italy and beyond. 🌐💼

### Master's Program in **Quantitative Methods for Economics and Finance**  
*Two Specializations: Economics & Finance*  

---

#### **Program Overview**  
This Master’s program equips students with advanced quantitative skills to analyze economic and financial systems, combining theoretical knowledge with practical applications. Graduates are prepared for leadership roles in public, private, and international contexts.  

---

#### **Specialization 1: Expert in Quantitative Economics**  
**Core Competencies:**  
- Advanced economic theory, macroeconomic analysis, and policy evaluation.  
- Statistical/mathematical tools for economic data analysis (e.g., forecasting, policy impact assessment).  
- Risk management and sustainability in economic systems.  
- Financial management of enterprises and public institutions.  
- Use of datasets for empirical economic research.  

**Key Job Roles:**  
- **Quantitative Economist** (e.g., analyzing market trends, fiscal policy impacts).  
- **Public Economic Officer** (e.g., designing economic strategies for government agencies).  
- **Economic Consultant** (e.g., advising businesses on market dynamics).  

**Typical Tasks:**  
- Conduct quantitative analysis of economic systems.  
- Evaluate direct/indirect impacts of corporate/public policies.  
- Link observed economic trends to theoretical models.  
- Support decision-making using econometric models.  

---

#### **Specialization 2: Expert in Quantitative Finance**  
**Core Competencies:**  
- Financial theory, portfolio management, and risk modeling.  
- Advanced statistical/mathematical tools for financial data (e.g., risk assessment, predictive analytics).  
- Financial regulations and market dynamics.  
- Management of financial datasets and scenario planning.  

**Key Job Roles:**  
- **Financial Analyst** (e.g., market analysis, investment strategies).  
- **Portfolio Manager** (e.g., optimizing asset allocation).  
- **Risk Manager** (e.g., assessing financial risks using quantitative models).  
- **Financial Consultant/Broker** (e.g., advising on complex financial products).  

**Typical Tasks:**  
- Apply quantitative tools to financial data for empirical analysis.  
- Develop predictive models for financial scenarios.  
- Design innovative tools for descriptive/predictive financial analysis.  
- Evaluate financial risks using statistical models.  

---

#### **Shared Program Features**  
- **Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors):**  
  - **Critical Analysis:** Independently assess economic/financial systems.  
  - **Communication:** Present findings in technical reports (English/Italian).  
  - **Autonomy:** Solve real-world problems using interdisciplinary knowledge.  
  - **Language:** **Italian** (primary instruction) and **English** (for technical materials and global collaboration).  

- **Practical Focus:**  
  - Case studies, data analysis (using real datasets), and group projects.  
  - Emphasis on **sustainability** (Economics track) and **financial innovation** (Finance track).  

---

#### **Career Pathways**  
| **Specialization**       | **Workplace Context**                          | **Global Relevance** |  
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------|  
| **Quantitative Economics** | Public institutions, international agencies (e.g., IMF), consulting firms. | High (policy-focused roles). |  
| **Quantitative Finance**   | Banks, asset management firms, fintech startups. | High (finance-driven roles). |  

---

#### **Why Choose This Program?**  
- **Dual Expertise:** Bridges economics *and* finance with advanced quantitative rigor.  
- **Industry Alignment:** Directly addresses demand for data-driven decision-making in both sectors.  
- **Global Readiness:** English proficiency ensures competitiveness in international markets.  

*Graduates are equipped to lead in complex economic/financial landscapes, leveraging data to shape strategy and policy.*

The **Master's Program in Business Consulting and Management** (Consulenza e Gestione di Impresa) is designed to equip students with advanced competencies for high-level roles in business consulting and corporate management, aligned with the **Dublin Descriptors** of the European Higher Education Area. Below is a concise overview of its key features:

---

### **Core Focus Areas**  
1. **Knowledge & Expertise**  
   - Mastery of **financial accounting (IAS/IFRS)**, strategic planning, risk management, social accounting, and crisis management (e.g., restructuring, bankruptcy).  
   - Proficiency in **business planning**, financial control, and integrated management systems.  
   - Understanding of **legal and fiscal frameworks** for corporate operations.  

2. **Professional Skills**  
   - Solving complex business challenges (e.g., corporate restructuring, financial risk assessment).  
   - Preparing **business plans** for new ventures or existing enterprises.  
   - Applying **technology-driven communication** tools for data presentation.  

3. **Communication & Collaboration**  
   - Ability to convey technical insights clearly to **experts and non-experts**.  
   - Working effectively in **international teams** (taught in **Italian and English**).  
   - Strong written/oral communication for professional reporting and presentations.  

4. **Lifelong Learning**  
   - Continuous updating on industry trends, regulatory changes, and digital tools.  
   - Preparation for **advanced studies** (e.g., PhD) or independent research.  

---

### **Career Paths**  
Graduates qualify for **two primary professional roles**:  

#### **1. High-Level Business Consultant**  
- **Certifications**: Eligible for **Dottore Commercialista** (Chartered Accountant) and **Esperto Contabile** (with State Exam, *fascia A*).  
- **Roles**:  
  - Corporate advisor for **extraordinary operations** (mergers, acquisitions, valuations).  
  - Expert in **financial reporting (IAS/IFRS)**, legal audits, and crisis management (e.g., bankruptcy, restructuring).  
  - Specialist in **social accounting** and **risk control**.  

#### **2. Functional Manager**  
- **Roles in large enterprises**:  
  - **Chief Financial Officer (CFO)**, **Risk Manager**, **Internal Control Director**.  
  - **Strategic roles**: Head of Planning & Control, General Manager, or Operational Analyst.  
  - **Public/private sector**: Leading corporate functions in multinational firms or public institutions.  

---

### **Program Highlights**  
- **Language**: Taught in **Italian and English**; international internships/study abroad opportunities.  
- **Prerequisites**: Builds on **bachelor’s-level business/economics knowledge** (e.g., accounting, management).  
- **Professional Integration**: Prepares students for **Italian professional registers** (*albo*) and global business standards.  
- **Final Assessment**: Includes a **thesis defense** evaluating analytical, research, and communication skills.  

---

### **Why This Program?**  
- **Unique Value**: Bridges **technical accounting expertise** with **strategic management** for leadership roles.  
- **Industry Demand**: Addresses needs in **financial consulting**, **corporate governance**, and **digital transformation**.  
- **Global Relevance**: Aligns with international standards (e.g., IAS/IFRS) for cross-border career mobility.  

This program is ideal for students aiming to **lead in corporate finance, consulting, or strategic management** within dynamic business environments.

### **Summary of the *Management d'Impresa* (Business Management) Degree Program**  
*(Italian Higher Education, Class L-18)*  

#### **Program Overview**  
This interdisciplinary program combines **business management, economics, law, and quantitative methods** to prepare students for dynamic roles in corporate, public, and non-profit sectors. Taught in **Italian and English**, it emphasizes practical skills through case studies, internships (*tirocinio*), and project-based learning.  

---

#### **Key Learning Outcomes**  
1. **Knowledge & Skills**  
   - Strategic management, marketing, financial control, quality management, supply chain operations.  
   - Economic analysis, legal frameworks, and data-driven decision-making.  
   - Ability to design and interpret business models (*e.g., for startups or corporate strategy*).  

2. **Communication & Collaboration**  
   - Fluent communication in Italian/English for presentations, reports, and team collaboration.  
   - Cross-cultural competence for international work environments.  

3. **Autonomy & Critical Thinking**  
   - Analyze complex business scenarios and propose innovative solutions.  
   - Develop independent research and problem-solving skills for advanced studies or professional growth.  

4. **Professional Readiness**  
   - Access to **Chartered Accountant (Dottore Commercialista)** exams (after passing the state exam) and **agro-technical certification**.  
   - Prepares for roles requiring regulatory compliance (e.g., financial audits, strategic consulting).  

---

#### **Career Opportunities**  
Graduates are equipped for **mid-to-senior roles** across sectors:  
- **Managerial Positions**:  
  - Operations, finance, marketing, and supply chain management in SMEs or large corporations.  
  - Leadership roles in small businesses (e.g., *direttore generale*) or mid-level management in complex organizations.  
- **Consulting**:  
  - Strategic, financial, or quality management consulting (*e.g., for corporate clients or public institutions*).  
- **Administrative Roles**:  
  - Economic, administrative, or operational support in **private, public, or non-profit sectors** (e.g., government agencies, NGOs, multinational firms).  

---

#### **Unique Value Proposition**  
- **Interdisciplinary Edge**: Blends business acumen with economics, law, and data analytics.  
- **Global Relevance**: English proficiency and international case studies prepare students for global markets.  
- **Regulatory Access**: Direct pathway to professional certifications (e.g., *Dottore Commercialista*), enhancing career mobility in Italy.  

---

**Ideal For**: Students seeking a **versatile, practice-oriented business degree** with strong career pathways in management, consulting, and cross-sector leadership. The program bridges academic rigor with real-world application, emphasizing adaptability in evolving business landscapes.

Status professionale conferito dal titolo.
Esperto nel settore Economico, Bancario e Finanziario Il Corso di laurea in EBF fornisce una preparazione orientata a sbocchi occupazionali e attività professionali, sia nel settore privato che pubblico. In particolare, il laureato potrà inserirsi:
- nell’ambito economico-finanziario in imprese di assicurazione, enti previdenziali, banche, società di intermediazione e gestione del risparmio.
- in società di consulenza finanziaria o assicurativa.
- in imprese non finanziarie.
- in amministrazioni (nazionali, regionali, locali) e aziende pubbliche, nonché in enti di ricerca.
- nell'ambito di uffici studi di organismi territoriali, sindacali e professionali.
Caratteristiche prova finale.
La prova finale consiste nella presentazione ad una apposita commissione di un elaborato scritto.
L'elaborato, redatto sotto la supervisione di un docente del corso di laurea, dovrà essere riferito ad una disciplina presente nel regolamento.
La discussione dell'elaborato di fronte alla commissione dovrà essere svolta in modo tale da permettere a quest'ultima di esprimere, alla luce degli obiettivi formativi propri del corso di laurea, anche una valutazione sul complessivo patrimonio di competenze raggiunto dal candidato.
In particolare, lo studente deve dimostrare di aver acquisito, oltre ad una adeguata conoscenza e comprensione del tema prescelto, anche autonoma capacità di apprendimento e di ricerca; capacità di utilizzare correttamente la letteratura consultata e le fonti dei dati necessarie; capacità di presentare e di sostenere argomentazioni scientifiche in modo logico e coerente.
Conoscenze richieste per l'accesso.
Per essere ammessi al Corso di laurea è necessario il possesso di Diploma di scuola media superiore di durata quinquennale o altro titolo di studio conseguito all'estero riconosciuto idoneo, o di Diploma di scuola media superiore di durata quadriennale e del relativo anno integrativo.
Per l'accesso al corso di laurea si richiedono, altresì, conoscenze di base in campo matematico, un sufficiente grado di abilità logico-matematiche e familiarità con gli strumenti informatici di uso comune. Tenuto conto dei caratteri del corso, è auspicabile l'attitudine ad assumere iniziative, la sistematicità, la capacità di argomentare e l'orientamento alla soluzione dei problemi.
Per il curriculum Economics è inoltre richiesta la buona conoscenza certificata della lingua inglese, corrispondente almeno al livello B1 del Quadro di riferimento delle lingue del Consiglio d’Europa.
Per le modalità di verifica di tali conoscenze, obbligatorie in base al DM 270/04, si rimandata al regolamento didattico del corso di studio, nel quale saranno altresì indicati gli obblighi formativi aggiuntivi previsti nel caso in cui la verifica non sia positiva.
Obiettivi formativi specifici.
I laureati nei corsi di laurea della classe devono:
•- possedere un'adeguata conoscenza delle discipline economiche ed essere dotati di adeguata padronanza degli strumenti matematico-statistici e dei principi e istituti dell'ordinamento giuridico;
•saper affrontare le problematiche proprie dei sistemi economici e delle aziende che ne costituiscono il tessuto;
• possedere una buona padronanza del metodo della ricerca, della metodica economica e delle tecniche proprie dei diversi settori di applicazione, tenendo anche conto delle innovazioni legate alle analisi di genere;
• possedere competenze pratiche ed operative, relative alla misura, al rilevamento ed al trattamento dei dati pertinenti l'analisi economica nei suoi vari aspetti applicativi;
• possedere un'adeguata conoscenza della cultura organizzativa dei contesti lavorativi;
• possedere adeguate competenze e strumenti per la comunicazione e la gestione dell'informazione.
Titolo di studio rilasciato.
Laurea in ECONOMIA, BANCA E FINANZA Descrittori di Dublino: I - Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione Economica I laureati del Corso di Laurea in EBF acquisiscono conoscenze e sviluppano capacità di comprensione in una serie di aree specifiche del campo economico. In particolare:
- Conoscono adeguatamente le basi metodologiche e concettuali della teoria economica, con particolare riferimento: a modelli introduttivi di economia politica, micro e macroeconomici;
- Conoscono elementi introduttivi della economia pubblica, della politica economica e dell’economia applicata;
- Apprendono gli elementi essenziali dell'inquadramento storico dei fenomeni economici;
- Sono in grado di utilizzare in maniera appropriata gli strumenti quantitativi in campo economico.
- Sviluppano una capacità di comprensione, interpretazione e analisi dei fenomeni economici e finanziari.
Aziendale I laureati del Corso di Laurea in EBF acquisiscono conoscenze e sviluppano capacità di comprensione in una serie di aree specifiche del campo aziendale. In particolare:
- Conoscono le basi metodologiche e concettuali dell'economia aziendale, con particolare riferimento alle aziende di credito ed agli intermediari finanziari;
- Apprendono i concetti fondamentali della tecnica bancaria;
- Sviluppano le abilità necessarie per la lettura dei bilanci;
- Conoscono gli elementi fondanti della gestione delle imprese e della finanza aziendale.
Statistico-Matematica I laureati del Corso di Laurea in EBF acquisiscono conoscenze e sviluppano capacità di comprensione in una serie di aree specifiche del campo statistico-matematico. In particolare:
- Conoscono gli strumenti statistico-matematici di base per l’analisi economica e finanziaria;
- Apprendono le tecniche computazionali per l'analisi dei dati;
- Sviluppano una capacità di analisi empirica dei fenomeni economici e finanziari.
Giuridica I laureati del Corso di Laurea in EBF acquisiscono conoscenze e sviluppano capacità di comprensione prevalentemente nelle seguenti aree del campo giuridico:
- Fondamenti del diritto privato;
- Fondamenti del diritto pubblico;
II - Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione Economica Le conoscenze teoriche e pratiche acquisite e l’analisi di casi studio permetteranno allo studente di:
- analizzare ed affrontare i temi chiave nei settori dell'economia finanziaria e dell'economia bancaria;
- identificare e trattare le implicazioni economiche delle diverse opzioni di politica economica;
- proporre soluzioni efficienti ed argomentate a problemi complessi di natura economica;
Tali attitudini verranno acquisite attraverso lo studio di casi pratici ed esercitazioni.
Aziendale Le conoscenze teoriche e pratiche acquisite e l’analisi di casi studio permetteranno allo studente di:
- analizzare ed affrontare i temi chiave nei settori dell'economia aziendale e della gestione delle imprese;
- conosce le principali aree operative delle banche;
Tali attitudini verranno acquisite attraverso lo studio di casi pratici ed esercitazioni.
Statistico-Matematica Le conoscenze teoriche e computazionali acquisite permetteranno allo studente di:
- decidere le strategie di analisi quantitativa più appropriate per affrontare temi di natura economico-finanziaria;
- affrontare l'analisi delle decisioni in condizioni di incertezza in campo economico-finanziario.
- scegliere le fonti statistiche e le basi di dati più adatte per la risoluzione di problemi empirici;
Tali attitudini verranno acquisite attraverso lo studio di casi pratici ed esercitazioni.
Giuridica Le conoscenze acquisite in campo giuridico permetteranno allo studente di:
- conoscere le nozioni fondamentali del diritto privato e pubblico;
- comprendere gli elementi di base del linguaggio tecnico-giuridico;
Tali attitudini verranno acquisite attraverso lo studio di casi pratici ed esercitazioni.
III - Autonomia di giudizio I laureati in Economia, Banca e Finanza acquisiscono abilità e competenze relative a:
- analizzare in modo critico i fenomeni economici e finanziari ed esprimere giudizi autonomi riguardo agli stessi,
- individuare ed utilizzare correttamente le fonti statistiche inerenti l'area economico-finanziaria.
- integrare le conoscenze economiche con una comprensione più ampia del funzionamento dei sistemi economico-sociali, avvalendosi degli apporti di tipo interdisciplinare (storici, istituzionali, giuridici) caratterizzanti il corso di laurea.
Gli obiettivi formativi sono conseguiti attraverso lo svolgimento delle diverse attività didattiche d'aula e di laboratorio e la preparazione della prova finale, oltre che eventuali esperienze formative esterne.
IV - Abilità comunicative Alla fine del corso di studio i laureati saranno in grado di:
- comunicare informazioni, idee, problemi e soluzioni in forma scritta ed orale a interlocutori specialisti e non specialisti;
- confrontarsi con gli altri, specialmente nell'elaborazione di progetti di gruppo;
- utilizzare in modo appropriato il linguaggio delle discipline economiche, finanziarie e quantitative.
- esprimersi correttamente in lingua inglese, in particolare con riferimento a tematiche economiche e finanziarie.
- scrivere e presentare brevi rapporti in termini chiari e concisi, anche in lingua inglese;
Le abilità comunicative sono sviluppate in occasione delle attività formative che prevedono la preparazione di relazioni e documenti scritti e la successiva presentazione orale. L'acquisizione di tali abilità avviene, inoltre, tramite l'attività svolta dallo studente per la preparazione della prova finale e/o la discussione della medesima.
La lingua inglese viene appresa tramite apposite attività formative e verificata mediante le relative prove d'esame.
Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione.
ITALIANO V - Capacità di apprendimento Il corso di laurea EBF fornisce allo studente le abilità di base necessarie allo studio autonomo dell'economia e della finanza, sia dal punto di vista teorico che da quello empirico-quantitativo.
Pertanto, alla fine del proprio percorso di studio, il laureato in EBF avrà acquisito le conoscenze sufficienti e la padronanza dei saperi necessari ad affrontare in modo adeguato gli studi universitari di II livello in campo economico e matematico-statistico.
Tale preparazione verrà acquisita dallo studente con la consuetudine allo studio, nonché attraverso le attività formative di supporto alla preparazione degli esami e della prova finale.
Competenze associate alla funzione.
Esperto nel settore Economico, Bancario e Finanziario Lo sbocco occupazionale principale dei neolaureati in EBF attiene a percorsi professionali in posizioni di tipo junior, sia nel settore privato in aziende bancarie, finanziarie e assicurative, sia nel settore pubblico nelle aree economica, gestionale e statistica.
Funzione in contesto di lavoro.
Esperto nel settore Economico, Bancario e Finanziario I laureati del Corso di Laurea in Economia, Banca e Finanza (EBF) acquisiscono conoscenze e sviluppano capacità di comprensione in una serie di aree specifiche:
- Conoscono le basi metodologiche e concettuali della teoria economica, con riferimento in particolare ai modelli introduttivi micro e macroeconomici; ad elementi introduttivi della politica economica e dell'economia pubblica; a elementi essenziali dell'inquadramento storico dei fenomeni economici;
- Conoscono le basi metodologiche e concettuali dell'economia aziendale;
- Conoscono i fondamenti del diritto privato e del diritto dell'economia;
- Conoscono gli strumenti matematico-statistici fondamentali per l'analisi economica e finanziaria.
La preparazione acquisita consentirà ai laureati di svolgere funzioni operative in vari contesti lavorativi, pubblici e privati, sia nazionali che internazionali. Il laureato, in particolare, possiederà le competenze necessarie per inserirsi in numerose posizioni lavorative di tipo impiegatizio e di supporto alla consulenza, anche in piccole e medie imprese, e per operare come esperto di analisi e governo di sistemi economici.

[1290] BUSINESS ECONOMICS Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

### Summary of the Three-Year Degree in Business Economics (Economia Aziendale)  
**Program Overview**  
This three-year undergraduate program (Laurea Triennale) in Business Economics equips students with interdisciplinary skills in **economic, legal, and quantitative analysis**, preparing them for roles in accounting, management, and financial decision-making. The curriculum combines theoretical knowledge with practical training through case studies, internships, and project work. All instruction and assessments are conducted in **Italian**.  

---

### **Core Competencies Developed**  
1. **Autonomy of Judgment**  
   - Ability to analyze economic, social, and business data using quantitative methods.  
   - Form independent opinions through critical reflection on complex business scenarios.  
   - *Verification*: Evaluated during internships and final thesis preparation.  

2. **Communication Skills**  
   - Clearly convey complex ideas to diverse audiences (e.g., clients, teams).  
   - Master active listening, cross-cultural collaboration, and professional English (basic proficiency required).  
   - *Verification*: Oral presentations, group projects, and final thesis defense.  

3. **Learning Ability**  
   - Develop self-directed learning habits for continuous professional growth (e.g., lifelong learning, research).  
   - *Verification*: Independent study, data analysis tasks, and final thesis.  

4. **Professional Expertise**  
   - Mastery of accounting, tax, financial analysis, and management systems.  
   - *Verification*: Practical exercises, internships, and case studies.  

---

### **Professional Career Paths**  
Graduates are prepared for **entry-level roles** in private, public, and non-profit organizations, with potential for advancement after field experience. Key roles include:  

#### **1. Accountant/Consultant (Esperto Contabile)**  
   - **Responsibilities**: Handle accounting, tax compliance, financial reporting, and strategic planning.  
   - **Professional Path**: Qualifies for **Category B of the "Esperto Contabile" register** (requires internship + state exam).  
   - **Skills**: General accounting, legal frameworks, tax systems.  

#### **2. Managerial Roles**  
   - **Administration & Accounting Manager**: Oversee financial operations in SMEs (after initial field experience).  
   - **Planning & Control Manager**: Lead strategic planning, budgeting, and performance analysis.  
   - **Finance Manager**: Analyze financial data, manage investments, and support decision-making.  
   - **Skills**: Data-driven decision-making, cross-departmental collaboration.  

#### **3. Administrative & Support Roles**  
   - **Work Context**: SMEs, public institutions, non-profits.  
   - **Responsibilities**: Manage day-to-day operations, financial documentation, and reporting.  
   - **Skills**: Organizational efficiency, communication, basic financial literacy.  

---

### **Key Notes**  
- **Language**: All coursework and assessments are in Italian.  
- **Professional Requirements**: To become a certified **Esperto Contabile**, graduates must complete an internship and pass a state exam (beyond the degree).  
- **Career Trajectory**: The degree provides foundational skills for immediate entry into the workforce, with opportunities for specialization (e.g., finance, tax consulting) after gaining experience.  

This program bridges academic rigor with real-world application, positioning graduates for dynamic careers in business and finance across Italy and beyond. 🌐💼

### **Summary of Core Competencies for a Medical and Surgical Graduate (Italy)**  
This summary distills the essential competencies required for a **Medico-Chirurgo** (Medical Doctor) in Italy, based on the national curriculum standards. It emphasizes clinical, public health, and professional skills, structured to align with modern healthcare demands.

---

#### **1. Clinical Practice Competencies**  
- **Holistic Patient Assessment**:  
  - Collect comprehensive clinical histories (including social/occupational factors).  
  - Perform thorough physical and mental health examinations.  
  - Interpret diagnostic results and apply evidence-based treatment strategies.  
- **Emergency & Critical Care**:  
  - Recognize life-threatening conditions and manage common medical emergencies autonomously.  
  - Prioritize patient safety and ethical care in all interventions.  
- **Patient-Centered Care**:  
  - Address physical, psychological, social, and cultural factors in treatment plans.  
  - Promote health prevention and avoid disease through personalized advice.  

---

#### **2. Public Health & Healthcare Systems**  
- **Population Health Determinants**:  
  - Analyze factors influencing health (lifestyle, genetics, environment, socio-economic status, migration, trade).  
  - Design preventive strategies for diseases, injuries, and public health crises.  
- **Global Health Awareness**:  
  - Monitor international health trends, chronic disease patterns, and the role of global organizations (e.g., WHO).  
- **Healthcare System Navigation**:  
  - Understand healthcare policies, funding, cost-efficiency, and equitable access to care.  
  - Use epidemiological and demographic data for evidence-based decision-making.  
- **Collaborative Leadership**:  
  - Work within multidisciplinary teams (e.g., nurses, specialists) and engage communities in health promotion.  
  - Advocate for systemic equity in healthcare delivery.  

---

#### **3. Professional & Interdisciplinary Skills**  
- **Integrated Approach**:  
  - Bridge basic sciences (e.g., biology, pharmacology) with clinical practice.  
  - Address clinical, relational, educational, social, and ethical dimensions of care.  
- **Communication & Cultural Competence**:  
  - Communicate clearly and compassionately with patients, families, and colleagues in multicultural settings.  
- **Lifelong Learning & Technology**:  
  - Manage medical information via digital tools (e.g., electronic health records, AI-assisted diagnostics).  
  - Critically evaluate new research and adapt to evolving medical practices.  

---

#### **4. Career Pathways**  
Graduates are qualified to work in:  
- **Public Sector**: SSN (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale) entities (hospitals, clinics, research institutes).  
- **Private Sector**: Private clinics, independent practice, or specialized medical centers.  
- **Advanced Training**: Eligible for specialization schools, research doctorates, or medical master’s programs.  

---

### **Key Differentiators**  
- **Ethical & Preventive Focus**: Prioritizes health promotion over reactive care.  
- **Global Mindset**: Integrates international health trends into local practice.  
- **Systemic Thinking**: Balances individual patient needs with population-level health outcomes.  

This framework ensures graduates are equipped to address complex health challenges while adhering to Italy’s healthcare standards and global best practices.

### Summary of the Master's Program in Rehabilitation Sciences  

This **two-year, Italian-taught program** prepares students for advanced roles in rehabilitation science, emphasizing **clinical expertise, leadership, interdisciplinary collaboration, and evidence-based practice**. Aligned with the **Dublin Descriptors** (European higher education standards), the curriculum is structured around five core competencies:  

---

#### **1. Knowledge & Clinical Application**  
- **Evidence-based rehabilitation**: Mastery of patient assessment, functional diagnosis, ethical/legal frameworks, and disability management.  
- **Interdisciplinary teamwork**: Integration of clinical, organizational, and managerial skills to optimize patient outcomes (e.g., multiprofessional case analysis, innovative intervention planning).  
- **Leadership & management**: Training in team coordination, resource allocation, quality assurance, and accreditation systems.  

---

#### **2. Autonomy & Critical Thinking**  
- Graduates develop **reflective decision-making** skills, evaluating the impact of their actions on patient care and organizational performance.  
- Ability to **critically analyze research** (clinical, management, educational) and apply findings to real-world scenarios.  
- Engagement in **interdisciplinary dialogue** (scientific, ethical, legal) to address complex rehabilitation challenges.  

---

#### **3. Communication & Cultural Competence**  
- **Effective communication** with patients, families, and healthcare teams across diverse age groups and cultural backgrounds.  
- **Mentorship & education**: Designing patient/family education programs, training healthcare professionals, and fostering collaborative leadership.  
- **Conflict resolution & negotiation**: Supporting team dynamics through adaptive management styles.  

---

#### **4. Lifelong Learning & Research**  
- **Self-directed learning**: Continuous professional development via self-assessment, literature reviews, and strategic planning.  
- **Research integration**: Conducting independent research (culminating in a thesis), analyzing global evidence, and disseminating findings.  
- **Digital literacy**: Using databases and software for evidence synthesis and knowledge management.  

---

#### **5. Practical Training & Assessment**  
- **Clinical internships**: Supervised practice in diverse healthcare settings (simple to complex), with structured debriefing sessions.  
- **Assessment methods**: Written/oral exams, case studies, practical reports, thesis defense, and reflective presentations.  
- **Focus on inclusivity**: Addressing cultural differences and tailoring communication to individual needs.  

---

### **Program Highlights**  
- **Language**: Taught entirely in **Italian**.  
- **Career outcomes**: Graduates lead rehabilitation teams, design educational programs, pursue research, or specialize in healthcare management.  
- **Unique focus**: Blends **clinical rigor** with **organizational leadership**, preparing students for evolving healthcare demands.  

This program equips professionals to deliver **patient-centered, culturally sensitive, and ethically grounded rehabilitation services** while driving innovation in the field.

### Summary of the Master's Program in Nursing and Midwifery (Italy)  
**Program Focus**: A two-year (biennale) Master’s program preparing graduates for **leadership and managerial roles** in healthcare (e.g., *Dirigente ed equiparati*), with specialization in **nursing and midwifery**.  

---

#### **Key Competencies Developed**  
1. **Clinical & Care Innovation**  
   - Critically assess evolving care needs (including gender-specific aspects).  
   - Design innovative care models and professional competency standards.  
   - Apply evidence-based practices to improve quality of care.  

2. **Management & Leadership**  
   - Plan, manage, and evaluate healthcare services with a focus on quality improvement.  
   - Collaborate on budgeting, staffing, and resource allocation.  
   - Lead multidisciplinary teams and resolve conflicts.  
   - Develop strategies to enhance staff satisfaction and retention.  

3. **Research & Evidence-Based Practice**  
   - Identify research gaps in clinical, organizational, and educational domains.  
   - Apply research findings to adapt care models to specific contexts.  
   - Use advanced IT systems to monitor clinical performance and workload.  

4. **Education & Training**  
   - Design and evaluate educational programs for all training levels (basic, advanced, continuous).  
   - Mentor students and professionals in clinical and organizational settings.  
   - Develop community-based health education initiatives for risk management.  

5. **Ethics & Multicultural Collaboration**  
   - Critically analyze ethical issues in care and interdisciplinary teamwork.  
   - Foster inclusive, patient-centered decision-making processes.  

---

#### **Professional Roles Post-Graduation**  
Graduates are qualified for **senior roles** in:  
- **Healthcare Management**: Leading nursing/midwifery departments, quality improvement, and strategic planning.  
- **Research**: Contributing to nursing/midwifery science through interdisciplinary projects.  
- **Education**: Designing curricula for nursing/midwifery training programs.  
- **Policy & Advocacy**: Shaping healthcare policies and standards.  

---

#### **Program Requirements**  
- **Language of Instruction**: **Italian** (all coursework, exams, and assessments conducted in Italian).  
- **Duration**: 2 years (biennale).  
- **Key Activities**:  
  - Clinical/practical internships with expert supervision.  
  - Development of research projects and evidence-based care proposals.  
  - Multidisciplinary collaboration in real-world healthcare settings.  

---

#### **Why This Program Stands Out**  
- Integrates **clinical excellence**, **managerial skills**, **research**, and **education** into a cohesive leadership framework.  
- Emphasizes **patient-centered care**, **quality improvement**, and **ethical decision-making**.  
- Prepares graduates for **national and international leadership roles** in healthcare systems.  

---

**Note for International Applicants**:  
- Proficiency in **Italian** is required for full participation.  
- Graduates meet Italian regulatory standards for **managerial positions** in public/private healthcare institutions.  

This program is ideal for nurses/midwives aiming to transition from clinical practice to **strategic leadership** in healthcare systems.
