Titolo di Scuola Superiore Ruoli Student mobility manager GIUSEPPE MANDAGLIO Presidente GIUSEPPE MANDAGLIO Coordinatore GIUSEPPE MANDAGLIO Programma, testi e obiettivi Status professionale conferito dal titolo.
Tecnico Fisico
- tecnico in grado di collaborare con specialisti nelle ricerche e nelle sperimentazioni di laboratorio nel campo della fisica, presso enti pubblici e privati in ambito industriale e di ricerca;
- tecnico in grado di collaborare con specialisti nel settore della produzione di energia per il controllo di apparati, impianti e dei relativi sistemi tecnici, garantendone il funzionamento e la sicurezza.
Caratteristiche prova finale.
La prova finale ha come obiettivo la produzione di un elaborato che tratta, con un grado di approfondimento adeguato al livello degli studi compiuti, o un argomento sviluppato durante il corso di studi oppure la realizzazione di un esperimento nell'ambito delle conoscenze di laboratorio acquisite.
La predisposizione e redazione dell'elaborato finale rappresenta un'attività formativa utile alla verifica del descrittore di Dublino relativo alla "Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione".
La presentazione dell'elaborato deve avvenire sotto forma di un breve seminario e il giudizio finale della Commissione di laurea dovrà tenere in considerazione sia la capacità di elaborazione personale dell'argomento che la coerenza tra obiettivi formativi attesi e conseguiti.
Conoscenze richieste per l'accesso.
Per l'ammissione al Corso di Laurea Triennale in Fisica si richiede il possesso del titolo di scuola secondaria superiore previsto dalla normativa in vigore o di altro titolo di studio conseguito all'estero, riconosciuto idoneo dagli organi competenti dell'Università.
Ai fini dell'accesso al corso di laurea in Fisica è richiesto allo studente il possesso delle seguenti conoscenze e competenze:
- buona padronanza della lingua italiana per comprendere e produrre testi e per descrivere problemi;
- capacità di utilizzare strutture logiche elementari;
- conoscenze matematiche a livello di scuola secondaria nel campo dell'Algebra, della Geometria euclidea e analitica e della Trigonometria.
La verifica della preparazione personale (ex art. 6, comma 1 del D.M. 270/04) viene effettuata con una modalità specificata nel Regolamento degli Studi.
Nel caso in cui la verifica della preparazione personale non sia positiva saranno assegnati degli obblighi formativi aggiuntivi (OFA) da soddisfare nel primo anno di corso.
Obiettivi formativi specifici.
Il Corso di Laurea in Fisica ha come obiettivo sia di formare laureati in grado di accedere direttamente ad attività lavorative in vari settori tecnologici che richiedono una definita familiarità con le metodologie scientifiche che dotati, al tempo stesso, di una preparazione che consenta loro un inserimento diretto in corsi di laurea magistrale.
In particolare, il corso si prefigge di fornire un adeguato bagaglio culturale e di sviluppare quelle capacità di ragionamento critico che permetteranno al laureato di:
1) inquadrare differenti fenomeni fisici e saperli rappresentare mediante modelli semplici ma al contempo efficaci in termini di variabili fisiche appropriate, sia dimensionalmente che quantitativamente;
2) impostare un problema utilizzando il corretto riferimento e trovarne una valida soluzione sulla base di opportune relazioni tra grandezze fisiche;
3) avere la capacità di utilizzare le teorie e i modelli consolidati in ambito fisico e saper affrontare semplici quesiti approntando risposte anche in termini probabilistici;
4) saper mettere a punto semplici configurazioni sperimentali ed essere in grado di effettuare la misurazione di parametri fisici corredandone il risultato con il relativo errore di misura;
5) saper utilizzare tutte quelle abilità trasversali (informatiche, linguistiche, ecc.) che permettano al laureato di effettuare le opportune elaborazioni e/o presentazioni di dati teorico-sperimentali, di consultare testi in lingua straniera e predisporre relazioni;
6) avere consapevolezza dei propri limiti e nel contempo aver maturato una capacità autonoma all'aggiornamento e all'approfondimento.
Il corso di studi prevede un unico percorso formativo, al cui interno sono presenti le seguenti aree di apprendimento:
1. Attività di base, in cui sono presenti l'area matematica, con l'obiettivo di fornire le conoscenze matematiche utilizzate nella indagine fisica, e l'area della fisica classica, con l'obiettivo di fornire le conoscenze fondamentali sia dal punto di vista teorico che da quello sperimentale;
2. Attività caratterizzanti, in cui sono presenti l'area della fisica teorica e della fisica moderna, con l'obiettivo di fornire le conoscenze fondamentali della meccanica quantistica e della relatività, ed un inquadramento teorico e sperimentale delle aree principali della fisica moderna (dalla fisica nucleare e subnucleare alla fisica atomica, molecolare e della materia condensata);
3. Attività affini, con l'obiettivo di fornire le principali conoscenze sui settori scientifici e tecnologici fondamentali per il lavoro del fisico (chimica, elettronica e informatica).
Tutti gli insegnamenti prevedono lezioni frontali, esercitazioni e/o attività di laboratorio. Le discipline di base sono offerte al primo anno e al secondo anno, gli insegnamenti che ricadono nelle attività caratterizzanti e che richiedono competenze propedeutiche, sono concentrati nella parte finale del secondo anno e nel terzo anno di corso. I contenuti propedeutici degli insegnamenti che ricadono nelle attività affini si svolgono nel primo anno e continuano nel secondo anno con lo scopo di fornire competenze più specializzate.
Le conoscenze e le competenze maturate durante il corso triennale sono verificate attraverso prove di esame orali anche in forma di seminario, esercitazioni pratiche con elaborazione e presentazione di relazioni di laboratorio.
Il CdS prevede al terzo anno altre attività quali tirocini formativi presso aziende, laboratori di ricerca e soggiorni di studio presso università estere, che sono finalizzate a porre lo studente in contatto con le realtà lavorative adeguate alla sua preparazione per un arricchimento professionale.
La prova finale consiste nella preparazione e presentazione di un elaborato su un argomento connesso con i corsi del piano di studi che non deve possedere necessariamente caratteri di originalità. Da essa deve emergere la maturità culturale e la capacità del laureando di elaborazione personale ed autonoma dell'argomento e la sua abilità nel comunicare efficacemente il tema affrontato.
Titolo di studio rilasciato.
Laurea in FISICA Descrittori di Dublino: I - Conoscenza e capacità di comprensione Al termine del corso di Laurea Triennale in Fisica, lo studente avrà acquisto attraverso lo studio e le conseguenti verifiche conoscenze su:
- i diversi settori della fisica classica e moderna, attraverso le discipline fisiche di ambito sperimentale, teorico e dei fondamenti della fisica, microfisico e della struttura della materia;
- la metodologia scientifica per il trattamento di grandi insiemi di dati, attraverso le discipline fisiche di ambito sperimentale ed applicativo;
- gli strumenti matematici ed informatici adeguati per la descrizione e la modellizzazione di sistemi fisici, attraverso le discipline di ambito matematico;
- le strumentazioni e delle tecnologie di laboratorio idonei alle indagini sperimentali, attraverso le discipline fisiche di ambito sperimentale ed applicativo.
Sarà quindi in grado di applicare le conoscenze per la comprensione dei fenomeni fisici, fronteggiando le sfide conoscitive, sociali e applicative in è cui coinvolta la fisica (teorica, sperimentale e applicata).
II - Capacità di applicare conoscenza e comprensione Lo studente laureato in Fisica Triennale sarà in grado di applicare le conoscenze acquisite per:
- la rappresentazione e modellizzazione della realtà fisica, attraverso le discipline di ambito fisico sperimentale ed applicativo, matematico, teorico e dei fondamenti della fisica
- la elaborazione di testi e allo sviluppo di argomentazioni scientifiche, in forma orale o scritta, in italiano e in inglese, attraverso le discipline di ambito sperimentale e applicativo, microfisico e di struttura della materia;
- la formulazione di ipotesi e alla risoluzione di problemi individuando la strategia migliore, attraverso le discipline di ambito teorico e dei fondamenti della fisica, sperimentale ed applicativo.
Ciò consentirà al laureato il pronto inserimento negli ambienti di lavoro, rendendolo capace di collaborare all'interno di work teams.
III - Autonomia di giudizio I laureati in Fisica devono
-possedere la capacità di valutare criticamente in termini di acquisizione, elaborazione ed interpretazione i dati ricavati sia per via teorica che per via sperimentale;
-saper percepire il piacere delle scoperte e delle teorie della fisica grazie ad una maturata consapevolezza;
-essere capaci di cogliere gli aspetti etici della ricerca considerando le eventuali ricadute in termini di protezione della salute e dell'ambiente.
Attività formative dedicate al raggiungimento dei risultati attesi:
1) lo studente viene educato a comprendere il significato fisico dei vari fenomeni illustrati nelle lezioni di fisica teorica e sperimentale;
2) lo studente viene incoraggiato nella formulazione di giudizi autonomi attraverso lo studio e l'approfondimento individuale e i successivi momenti di confronto durante l'attività di tutorato;
3) le attività di tirocinio completano il percorso formativo finalizzato al conseguimento degli obiettivi proposti.
Modalità di verifica del risultato:
1) le prove di esame e di verifica intermedia permettono di esprimere una corretta valutazione delle sviluppate attitudini critiche, soprattutto in relazione a quelle questioni che pur non esplicitamente affrontate durante i corsi possono trovare soluzione in termini di una maturata consapevolezza critica;
2) la qualità e il grado di approfondimento delle tematiche relative all'elaborato finale consentono di esprimere una valutazione completa sul grado di autonomia di giudizio raggiunto.
IV - Abilità comunicative I laureati in Fisica devono
-essere in grado di presentare argomenti di Fisica sia di carattere divulgativo che di tipo tecnico, calibrando opportunamente la forma e i contenuti per renderli accessibili ad ogni tipologia di interlocutore;
-essere capaci di lavorare all'interno di gruppi eterogenei, di operare con definiti gradi di autonomia e di inserirsi prontamente negli ambienti di lavoro.
Attività formative dedicate al raggiungimento dei risultati attesi:
1) l'acquisizione di competenze informatiche, di specifiche abilità linguistiche e delle materie affini o integrative e a scelta libera per un totale di circa 45 CFU;
2) attività formative svolte attraverso attività di tutorato e seminariale;
3) attività di tirocinio: inserimento, sia pure per periodi di tempo limitati, in ambienti di lavoro.
Modalità di verifica del risultato:
1) valutazione della capacità espositiva sia durante le prove di esame che durante la presentazione dell'elaborato finale;
2) valutazione di relazioni ed elaborati, ivi compreso quello finale, che prevedono l'elaborazione e la presentazione di dati sperimentali e/o teorici, l'utilizzo di testi avanzati (anche in lingua inglese) insieme all'uso di conoscenze trasversali che hanno applicazioni in contesti più ampi.
Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione.
ITALIANO V - Capacità di apprendimento I laureati in Fisica devono
-essere in grado di apprendere nuovi argomenti di letteratura scientifica al fine di seguire l'innovazione e lo sviluppo della conoscenza per l'allargamento delle proprie competenze;
-essere capaci di fare ricerche consultando testi, riviste scientifiche ed archivi elettronici disponibili anche on line e in inglese, sviluppando la necessaria capacità di selezione dell'informazione.
Attività formative dedicate al raggiungimento dei risultati attesi.
Per "imparare ad imparare" agli studenti vengono offerti, sin dal primo anno, diversi supporti:
1) nell'ambito del servizio di tutorato, informazioni relative alle metodologie di studio da adottare;
2) accesso a risorse bibliografiche sia di tipo cartaceo che elettronico;
3) corsi per lo sviluppo delle abilità informatiche e delle conoscenze linguistiche;
4) cicli di seminari divulgativi su argomenti di ricerca attuale.
Modalità di verifica del risultato:
1) valutazione del metodo di studio attraverso gli esami scritti e orali;
2) valutazione dell'apprendimento di argomenti proposti per lo studio autonomo in connessione con specifiche prove di valutazione in itinere.
Competenze associate alla funzione.
Tecnico Fisico
- applica il metodo scientifico nell'analisi, rappresentazione e modellizzazione di sistemi fisici anche complessi;
- utilizza tecnologie informatiche in rapporto alla elaborazione e presentazione di dati e di risultati numerici sperimentali o derivanti da simulazioni;
- propone soluzioni a nuovi problemi;
- prepara e presenta ricerche scientifiche e/o materiali divulgativi, in forma orale o scritta, in italiano e in inglese;
- utilizza strumenti di auto-apprendimento per un aggiornamento rapido allineato al progresso della scienza e della tecnologia;
- ha capacità di lavorare in gruppo e si inserisce in un contesto lavorativo organizzato, riconoscendo ruoli e responsabilità.
Funzione in contesto di lavoro.
Tecnico Fisico
- Osserva e misura le proprietà fisiche, gli eventi e i cambiamenti. Li documenta e li registra in modo sistematico e attendibile;
- Elabora ed analizza i dati derivanti dalle osservazioni e dalle misure in laboratorio e li mette in relazione con teorie appropriate;
- Interviene nella soluzione di vari problemi scientifici e tecnologici, applicando le proprie conoscenze relative all'area fisica di base;
- Coadiuva le attività di ricerca, di controllo dei processi industriali e di analisi in aziende pubbliche e private;
- Svolge attività professionale in ambito delle applicazioni tecnologiche a livello industriale;
- Partecipa all'attività di centri di ricerca pubblici e privati sia a livello gestionale che curando le attività di modellizzazione ed di analisi di sistemi complessi. Cura inoltre le implicazioni informatico-fisiche.

COURSE: [9218] MATHEMATICS
SECTION: General Description

[9218] MATHEMATICS Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

**Program Overview**  
- **Degree Title**: Bachelor of Mathematics (Laurea Triennale in MATEMATICA)  
- **Duration**: 3 years (180 ECTS credits)  
- **Language of Instruction**: Italian (with emphasis on English proficiency for academic texts)  
- **Focus**: Combines theoretical mathematics with practical problem-solving, emphasizing modeling, computational tools, and interdisciplinary applications.  

---

**Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors)**  

**I. Knowledge and Understanding**  
- Mastery of core mathematical disciplines: algebra, calculus (single/multi-variable), statistics, probability, mathematical physics, numerical analysis, and computational methods.  
- Ability to read and interpret advanced mathematical texts in English.  
- *Assessment*: Written/oral exams, tutorials, and language training.  

**II. Application of Knowledge**  
- Solve mathematical problems across diverse fields, formalize real-world problems into mathematical models, and use computational tools (e.g., specialized software) for data analysis.  
- *Assessment*: Problem-solving exercises, project work, and software-based assignments.  

**III. Critical Judgment**  
- Construct logical arguments, evaluate proofs, analyze interdisciplinary models, and collaborate effectively in team settings.  
- *Assessment*: Exams, seminar presentations, thesis development, and internship evaluations.  

**IV. Communication Skills**  
- Present mathematical concepts clearly in Italian and English (written/oral) to both specialized and general audiences.  
- *Assessment*: Seminar presentations, thesis defense, language courses, and internship reports.  

**V. Learning Ability**  
- Pursue advanced studies (e.g., master’s programs) or adapt to evolving workplace demands in technical fields.  
- *Assessment*: Exams, group projects, internships, and thesis work.  

---

**Degree Title and Associated Competencies**  
- **Title**: Bachelor of Mathematics (Tecnico Matematico)  
- **Key Competencies**:  
  - Advanced analytical and modeling skills for theoretical and applied problems.  
  - Proficiency in data processing, logical reasoning, and numerical methods.  
  - Ability to translate complex problems into structured solutions.  

---

**Job Role in Professional Context**  
- **Title**: Mathematical Technician (Tecnico Matematico)  
- **Workplace Applications**:  
  - Provide technical support in economic/financial, IT, industrial, and technological sectors.  
  - Develop data-driven solutions, optimize processes, and model real-world scenarios.  
- **Core Skills**: Problem-solving, interdisciplinary collaboration, computational analysis, and clear communication.  

---  
*This program prepares graduates for immediate employment in technical roles or further academic study, with a strong emphasis on practical application and adaptability.*

-----

[9215] INFORMATICA Bachelor's Degree Course English Italian

-----

### **Computer Science Degree Program: Summary**  

#### **Program Overview**  
This Computer Science degree prepares students for specialized roles in software development, system administration, and data analysis. The curriculum integrates **theoretical knowledge** with **practical application**, culminating in a thesis with **two components**:  
- **Theoretical** (conceptual framework, critical analysis).  
- **Practical** (real-world implementation, project development).  
The program emphasizes **internships/stage** to bridge academic learning with industry experience.  

---

#### **Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors)**  
1. **Knowledge & Understanding (I)**  
   - Mastery of foundational concepts in programming, algorithms, data structures, and mathematical/statistical methods.  
2. **Application (II)**  
   - Ability to solve complex problems using appropriate programming paradigms, tools, and technologies.  
3. **Critical Thinking (III)**  
   - Evaluate solutions critically, identify anomalies, and propose innovative approaches to interdisciplinary challenges.  
4. **Communication (IV)**  
   - Present technical solutions to diverse audiences (specialized/general) in **Italian and English**; collaborate effectively in cross-functional teams.  
5. **Lifelong Learning (V)**  
   - Adapt to evolving technologies, pursue advanced studies, and apply skills in dynamic work environments.  

---

#### **Key Competencies & Job Roles**  
| **Role**                     | **Core Responsibilities**                                                                 | **Required Skills**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Analyst Programmer**       | Develop software end-to-end: analyze requirements, design, code, test, and validate solutions. | Programming languages, algorithm design, critical analysis of software correctness. |
| **System Administrator**     | Design, maintain, and secure networked systems; manage infrastructure, databases, and cloud platforms. | OS/networking, cybersecurity, database management, continuous learning.             |
| **Data Analyst**             | Collect, structure, and analyze data to drive data-driven decisions; apply statistical/mathematical models. | Data collection, statistical analysis, programming (Python/R), visualization tools. |

---

#### **Teaching & Assessment**  
- **Languages**: Courses and assessments delivered in **Italian and English**.  
- **Methods**:  
  - Lab-based projects, problem-solving exercises, and thesis work.  
  - Presentations, peer reviews, and industry collaboration (e.g., company meetings).  
- **Assessment**:  
  - Written/oral exams, project submissions, thesis defense, and internship evaluations.  

---

#### **Career Alignment**  
Graduates are equipped to excel in **high-demand roles** requiring:  
- **Technical proficiency** (e.g., coding, system architecture, data modeling).  
- **Adaptability** to emerging technologies (e.g., AI, cloud computing, big data).  
- **Professional communication** for cross-disciplinary collaboration.  

This program ensures graduates meet industry standards for **Analyst Programmers**, **System Administrators**, and **Data Analysts**, with a strong foundation in both **theory** and **real-world application**.

[2011] VETERINARY MEDICINE Master's Degree Single Cycle 5 Years

-----

**Summary of the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine (Italy)**  

This 5-year Master's program (Laurea Magistrale a ciclo unico) prepares graduates for comprehensive veterinary practice, aligning with European Association for Veterinary Education (EAEVE) standards and "day-one skills" for immediate professional readiness. The curriculum integrates **clinical medicine** (companion, equine, and exotic animals), **public health**, **food safety**, and **livestock production systems**, ensuring graduates meet national and EU regulatory frameworks.  

**Key Learning Outcomes:**  
- **Autonomy of Judgment:** Ability to diagnose, formulate treatment plans, and implement urgent legislative measures to protect animal and public health.  
- **Communication Skills:** Clear, scientific communication in Italian and English for diverse audiences (specialists, institutions, industry).  
- **Lifelong Learning:** Capacity to independently update knowledge through international databases and adapt to evolving regulations.  
- **Professional Competencies:** Mastery of clinical diagnostics, epidemiology, food chain safety, zootecnical consultancy, and animal welfare in research.  

**Professional Roles:**  
1. **Private Sector:**  
   - Clinical practice for companion/livestock animals.  
   - Independent consultancy for farms, feed/pharma industries, and food safety.  
   - Animal welfare oversight in research.  
2. **Public Sector (SSN - National Health Service):**  
   - Leadership roles (e.g., Director General for animal health, food safety management).  
   - Oversight of official testing laboratories and public health surveillance.  

**Core Focus Areas:**  
- **Clinical Medicine:** Full diagnostic and therapeutic workflows for diverse species.  
- **Public Health:** Disease prevention, epidemiological risk management, and food safety protocols.  
- **Production Systems:** Optimizing livestock health, nutrition, genetics, and sustainable farming.  

Graduates are equipped to address complex challenges in animal health, food security, and environmental sustainability, adhering to Italian and EU legislation while contributing to global veterinary standards.

[2016] SAFETY AND QUALITY OF ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS Master's Degree Course

-----

**Summary of the Master's Program in "Safety and Quality of Animal Production" (University of Messina)**  

This Master’s program, offered by the University of Messina’s Department of Veterinary Sciences, focuses on ensuring **safety and quality throughout the animal production supply chain** (from farming to processing). It adopts a holistic "chain approach," integrating **animal welfare, zoonoses, hygiene, and food safety** across all production stages.  

**Key Features:**  
- **Teaching Methodology:** Combines theory (70%) with **30% practical activities**, including field visits, lab work, and mandatory internships in agro-zootecnic enterprises, feed mills, food processing plants, and laboratories.  
- **Learning Outcomes:** Graduates develop **critical thinking, communication skills, and applied expertise** to address challenges in animal production, quality management, and food safety.  
- **Career Paths:** Prepares students for roles such as **Production Manager, Quality Assurance Specialist, Feed Consultant, Researcher**, or **Certification Consultant** in animal-derived food industries.  
- **Professional Recognition:** Qualifies graduates for the **"Zoonomo" sector** of the *Albo Professionale dei Dottori Agronomi e Forestali* (Agronomists and Foresters Register), enabling specialized work in animal production safety and quality.  
- **Thesis & Internship:** The thesis can be conducted during the internship (with industry partners) or at national/international institutions, enhancing practical and research skills.  

**Language:** Instruction and assessments are in **Italian**.  
**Unique Focus:** Bridges academic knowledge with industry needs, emphasizing **real-world problem-solving** in animal production and food safety.  

*Ideal for students aiming to lead in sustainable, safe, and high-quality animal food production systems.*

[2025] AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR ECOLOGICAL TRANSITION Bachelor's Degree Program

-----

### **Summary of the Bachelor's Program in *Scienze e Tecnologie Agrarie per la Transizione Ecologica* (Agricultural Sciences and Technologies for Ecological Transition)**  

This **first-level agronomist program** (Dottore Agronomo di primo livello) prepares graduates to address the challenges of **sustainable agriculture** and **ecological transition** through a **multidisciplinary, eco-centric approach**. Aligned with EU policies (e.g., Green Deal, organic farming regulations), the curriculum integrates **agronomy, animal science, environmental management, and business economics** to balance food production with biodiversity preservation and resource conservation.  

---

### **Key Competencies Developed**  
Graduates will master:  
1. **Sustainable Production Techniques**:  
   - Ecocompatible crop management, pest/disease control, and animal welfare practices.  
   - Precision farming, soil fertility enhancement, and low-impact agricultural systems.  
2. **Environmental Stewardship**:  
   - Biodiversity conservation (vegetal/animal), soil protection, and slope stability for terraced farming.  
   - EU regulatory frameworks (e.g., organic farming, biodiversity valorization).  
3. **Business & Innovation**:  
   - Management of horticultural, ornamental, and arboreal enterprises.  
   - Supply chain optimization, product valorization, and sustainability protocol design.  
4. **Technical & Engineering Skills**:  
   - Agricultural mechanization, irrigation systems, rural construction, and environmental asset valuation.  

---

### **Professional Opportunities**  
Graduates are equipped to work in **public and private sectors**, including:  
- **Technical Consulting**: For farms, agri-food companies, and environmental agencies.  
- **Sustainability Management**: Designing eco-friendly production systems and certification (e.g., organic, sustainability labels).  
- **Territorial Development**: Planning sustainable rural landscapes and stabilizing slope-based agricultural sites.  
- **Public Administration**: Supporting EU-funded ecological transition projects (e.g., CAP, LIFE Program).  
- **Junior Agronomist Roles**: Independent practice, farm management, or roles in agri-tech startups.  

---

### **Unique Program Features**  
- **EU Policy Integration**: Direct focus on European regulations for biodiversity and organic farming.  
- **Hands-On Learning**: Mandatory internships (*tirocinio/stage*) with industry leaders, guided by academic and corporate mentors.  
- **Communication & Digital Skills**: Training in technical communication (including English terminology), data-driven decision-making, and modern presentation tools.  
- **Lifecycle Perspective**: Covers the full agri-food chain—from production to transformation, marketing, and environmental impact assessment.  

---

### **Why This Program Stands Out**  
Unlike traditional agronomy degrees, this program **centers ecological transition as its core mission**, preparing graduates to lead the shift toward **climate-resilient, biodiversity-friendly agriculture** while meeting EU sustainability targets. Graduates are not just technicians but **strategic change agents** in the evolving agri-food sector.  

*Note: The program qualifies graduates for the Italian *Dottore Agronomo di primo livello* title, enabling direct entry into professional roles in agriculture, environmental management, and sustainable development.*

[2026] VETERINARY BIOTECHNOLOGY Master's Degree Program

-----

### **Master's Program in Veterinary Biotechnology: Key Overview**  
**Language of Instruction & Assessment:** Italian  

---

#### **Core Focus Areas**  
1. **Translational Medicine & Biotechnology**:  
   - Development of innovative therapeutic products for animal health.  
   - Use of animal models in biomedical research and cell therapy.  
2. **Animal Reproduction & Biodiversity**:  
   - Genetic selection, conservation of endangered species, and sustainable livestock production.  
3. **Diagnostics & Zoonotic Disease Control**:  
   - Molecular diagnostics, parasitology, and pharmacovigilance for veterinary drugs.  
4. **Ethical & Societal Impact**:  
   - Critical evaluation of biotechnological innovations on animal welfare, biodiversity, and public health.  

---

#### **Learning Outcomes (Master’s Competencies)**  
| **Descriptor**               | **Key Skills**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **I. Critical Judgment**     | Design research, analyze operational challenges, assess ethical/societal impacts of biotech innovations. |
| **II. Communication**        | Present complex scientific concepts to specialists and non-specialists (e.g., industry, policymakers). |
| **III. Autonomous Learning** | Conduct independent research using digital databases, update professional knowledge via continuous learning. |
| **IV. Professional Application** | Apply biotech tools in diagnostics, therapeutics, and biodiversity preservation. |

---

#### **Teaching & Assessment Methods**  
- **Practical Training**: Lab work, internships in biotech firms, diagnostic labs, and pharmaceutical industries.  
- **Exams**: Written/oral tests, technical reports, presentations (using digital tools).  
- **Workshops & Seminars**: Collaborative projects, case studies on real-world biotech challenges.  

---

#### **Professional Roles (Post-Graduation)**  
| **Role**                     | **Key Responsibilities**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Therapeutic Specialist**   | Develop and test novel therapeutics for animal diseases; use animal models in biomedical research. |
| **Project Manager**          | Manage R&D projects, patent development, and industrial applications of diagnostic/therapeutic tools. |
| **Diagnostic Expert**        | Operate molecular diagnostics, analyze genetic variability, and monitor zoonotic disease spread. |
| **Biodiversity & Reproduction Specialist** | Preserve endangered species, optimize breeding programs, and ensure genetic diversity in livestock. |

---

#### **Unique Program Highlights**  
- **Interdisciplinary Approach**: Combines veterinary medicine, biotechnology, ethics, and industry collaboration.  
- **Industry Alignment**: Prepares graduates for roles in biotech firms, pharmaceutical companies, diagnostic labs, and conservation organizations.  
- **Global Relevance**: Addresses zoonotic diseases, sustainable agriculture, and biodiversity loss—critical global challenges.  

---

**Target Audience**:  
Students aiming for careers in veterinary biotechnology, translational medicine, animal health innovation, and biodiversity conservation.  

**Note**: Program is taught entirely in Italian, requiring proficiency for full engagement. Graduates are equipped to contribute to both scientific advancement and societal well-being through evidence-based biotech solutions.

[2015] SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND SAFETY OF ANIMAL PRODUCTION Bachelor's Degree

-----

### **Program Summary: Sciences and Technologies of Animal Production and Food Safety**  
*(Scienze e Tecnologie delle Produzioni Animali e Sicurezza Alimentare)*  

**Degree Level**: Bachelor’s (Laurea)  
**Language of Instruction**: Italian (with mandatory English proficiency for professional communication).  

---

### **Core Focus Areas**  
This program integrates **animal production systems**, **food safety**, **quality control**, and **sustainability** across the entire food supply chain—from livestock farming to processing and distribution. Key themes include:  
- **Technical & Economic Management**: Optimizing production efficiency while ensuring hygiene and cost-effectiveness in agro-zootechnical enterprises.  
- **Food Safety & Quality**: Implementing protocols for animal welfare, product safety, and environmental impact assessment (e.g., reducing ecological footprint in production chains).  
- **Regulatory Compliance**: Adhering to EU standards for food safety (e.g., HACCP, traceability) and animal welfare regulations.  

---

### **Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors)**  
Graduates will demonstrate:  
1. **Knowledge Application**: Use of scientific methods to solve technical problems in animal production and food processing (e.g., feed analysis, meat quality control).  
2. **Critical Judgment**: Ability to interpret data (lab/field) and address ethical/social issues (e.g., sustainable farming vs. resource use).  
3. **Communication**: Clear articulation of technical concepts to both specialists (e.g., industry partners) and non-specialists (e.g., consumers).  
4. **Lifelong Learning**: Capacity to adapt to evolving industry standards through continuous education (e.g., EU food safety updates).  

---

### **Practical Training**  
- **Internships (Stage)**: Mandatory placements in:  
  - Animal farms, slaughterhouses, and food processing plants (e.g., dairies, meat factories).  
  - Quality control labs (testing feed, raw materials, and final products).  
  - Public/private research institutions.  
- **Simulations & E-Learning**: Virtual tools for scenario-based problem-solving (e.g., outbreak management in food supply chains).  

---

### **Career Opportunities**  
Graduates qualify for roles in:  
- **Production & Processing**:  
  - *Quality Manager* (e.g., in cheese factories, salumerie).  
  - *Animal Welfare Officer* (safeguarding humane practices during slaughter).  
  - *Technical Advisor* for feed companies or livestock farms.  
- **Regulation & Certification**:  
  - *Supply Chain Auditor* (certifying production chains for safety/compliance).  
  - *Food Safety Specialist* in retail (e.g., large supermarkets, distributors).  
- **Research & Innovation**:  
  - Roles in public/private R&D centers (e.g., developing eco-friendly feed, renewable energy from agricultural waste).  

---

### **Professional Classification**  
Aligned with Italian professional categories:  
- **3.1**: Technical roles in scientific/engineering fields (e.g., food technology).  
- **3.2**: Technical roles in health/safety (e.g., food safety management).  

---

### **Why This Program?**  
- **Holistic Approach**: Bridges animal husbandry, food safety, and sustainability—addressing modern industry demands.  
- **Industry Relevance**: Directly prepares students for EU-regulated roles in a $1.5T global food sector.  
- **Global Readiness**: English proficiency ensures competitiveness in international markets (e.g., EU export standards).  

*Note: Graduates may pursue master’s degrees in food science, veterinary medicine, or agricultural economics for advanced roles.*  

---  
**Ideal for**: Students passionate about ethical food systems, animal welfare, and the science behind safe, sustainable food production. 🌱🐄🔬

[2011] VETERINARY MEDICINE Master's Degree Single Cycle 5 Years

-----

**Summary of the Master's Degree in Veterinary Medicine (Italy)**  

This 5-year Master's program (Laurea Magistrale a ciclo unico) prepares graduates for comprehensive veterinary practice, aligning with European Association for Veterinary Education (EAEVE) standards and "day-one skills" for immediate professional readiness. The curriculum integrates **clinical medicine** (companion, equine, and exotic animals), **public health**, **food safety**, and **livestock production systems**, ensuring graduates meet national and EU regulatory frameworks.  

**Key Learning Outcomes:**  
- **Autonomy of Judgment:** Ability to diagnose, formulate treatment plans, and implement urgent legislative measures to protect animal and public health.  
- **Communication Skills:** Clear, scientific communication in Italian and English for diverse audiences (specialists, institutions, industry).  
- **Lifelong Learning:** Capacity to independently update knowledge through international databases and adapt to evolving regulations.  
- **Professional Competencies:** Mastery of clinical diagnostics, epidemiology, food chain safety, zootecnical consultancy, and animal welfare in research.  

**Professional Roles:**  
1. **Private Sector:**  
   - Clinical practice for companion/livestock animals.  
   - Independent consultancy for farms, feed/pharma industries, and food safety.  
   - Animal welfare oversight in research.  
2. **Public Sector (SSN - National Health Service):**  
   - Leadership roles (e.g., Director General for animal health, food safety management).  
   - Oversight of official testing laboratories and public health surveillance.  

**Core Focus Areas:**  
- **Clinical Medicine:** Full diagnostic and therapeutic workflows for diverse species.  
- **Public Health:** Disease prevention, epidemiological risk management, and food safety protocols.  
- **Production Systems:** Optimizing livestock health, nutrition, genetics, and sustainable farming.  

Graduates are equipped to address complex challenges in animal health, food security, and environmental sustainability, adhering to Italian and EU legislation while contributing to global veterinary standards.

[2016] SAFETY AND QUALITY OF ANIMAL PRODUCTIONS Master's Degree Program

-----

**Summary of the Master's Program in "Safety and Quality of Animal Production" (University of Messina)**  

This Master’s program, offered by the University of Messina’s Department of Veterinary Sciences, focuses on ensuring **safety and quality throughout the animal production supply chain** (from farming to processing). It adopts a holistic "chain approach," integrating **animal welfare, zoonoses, hygiene, and food safety** across all production stages.  

**Key Features:**  
- **Teaching Methodology:** Combines theory (70%) with **30% practical activities**, including field visits, lab work, and mandatory internships in agro-zootecnic enterprises, feed mills, food processing plants, and laboratories.  
- **Learning Outcomes:** Graduates develop **critical thinking, communication skills, and applied expertise** to address challenges in animal production, quality management, and food safety.  
- **Career Paths:** Prepares students for roles such as **Production Manager, Quality Assurance Specialist, Feed Consultant, Researcher**, or **Certification Consultant** in animal-derived food industries.  
- **Professional Recognition:** Qualifies graduates for the **"Zoonomo" sector** of the *Albo Professionale dei Dottori Agronomi e Forestali* (Agronomists and Foresters Register), enabling specialized work in animal production safety and quality.  
- **Thesis & Internship:** The thesis can be conducted during the internship (with industry partners) or at national/international institutions, enhancing practical and research skills.  

**Language:** Instruction and assessments are in **Italian**.  
**Unique Focus:** Bridges academic knowledge with industry needs, emphasizing **real-world problem-solving** in animal production and food safety.  

*Ideal for students aiming to lead in sustainable, safe, and high-quality animal food production systems.*

[2025] AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR ECOLOGICAL TRANSITION Bachelor's Degree Program

-----

### **Summary of the Bachelor's Program in *Scienze e Tecnologie Agrarie per la Transizione Ecologica* (Agricultural Sciences and Technologies for Ecological Transition)**  

This **first-level agronomist program** (Dottore Agronomo di primo livello) prepares graduates to address the challenges of **sustainable agriculture** and **ecological transition** through a **multidisciplinary, eco-centric approach**. Aligned with EU policies (e.g., Green Deal, organic farming regulations), the curriculum integrates **agronomy, animal science, environmental management, and business economics** to balance food production with biodiversity preservation and resource conservation.  

---

### **Key Competencies Developed**  
Graduates will master:  
1. **Sustainable Production Techniques**:  
   - Ecocompatible crop management, pest/disease control, and animal welfare practices.  
   - Precision farming, soil fertility enhancement, and low-impact agricultural systems.  
2. **Environmental Stewardship**:  
   - Biodiversity conservation (vegetal/animal), soil protection, and slope stability for terraced farming.  
   - EU regulatory frameworks (e.g., organic farming, biodiversity valorization).  
3. **Business & Innovation**:  
   - Management of horticultural, ornamental, and arboreal enterprises.  
   - Supply chain optimization, product valorization, and sustainability protocol design.  
4. **Technical & Engineering Skills**:  
   - Agricultural mechanization, irrigation systems, rural construction, and environmental asset valuation.  

---

### **Professional Opportunities**  
Graduates are equipped to work in **public and private sectors**, including:  
- **Technical Consulting**: For farms, agri-food companies, and environmental agencies.  
- **Sustainability Management**: Designing eco-friendly production systems and certification (e.g., organic, sustainability labels).  
- **Territorial Development**: Planning sustainable rural landscapes and stabilizing slope-based agricultural sites.  
- **Public Administration**: Supporting EU-funded ecological transition projects (e.g., CAP, LIFE Program).  
- **Junior Agronomist Roles**: Independent practice, farm management, or roles in agri-tech startups.  

---

### **Unique Program Features**  
- **EU Policy Integration**: Direct focus on European regulations for biodiversity and organic farming.  
- **Hands-On Learning**: Mandatory internships (*tirocinio/stage*) with industry leaders, guided by academic and corporate mentors.  
- **Communication & Digital Skills**: Training in technical communication (including English terminology), data-driven decision-making, and modern presentation tools.  
- **Lifecycle Perspective**: Covers the full agri-food chain—from production to transformation, marketing, and environmental impact assessment.  

---

### **Why This Program Stands Out**  
Unlike traditional agronomy degrees, this program **centers ecological transition as its core mission**, preparing graduates to lead the shift toward **climate-resilient, biodiversity-friendly agriculture** while meeting EU sustainability targets. Graduates are not just technicians but **strategic change agents** in the evolving agri-food sector.  

*Note: The program qualifies graduates for the Italian *Dottore Agronomo di primo livello* title, enabling direct entry into professional roles in agriculture, environmental management, and sustainable development.*

[2026] VETERINARY BIOTECHNOLOGY Master's Degree Program

-----

### **Master's Program in Veterinary Biotechnology: Key Overview**  
**Language of Instruction & Assessment:** Italian  

---

#### **Core Focus Areas**  
1. **Translational Medicine & Biotechnology**:  
   - Development of innovative therapeutic products for animal health.  
   - Use of animal models in biomedical research and cell therapy.  
2. **Animal Reproduction & Biodiversity**:  
   - Genetic selection, conservation of endangered species, and sustainable livestock production.  
3. **Diagnostics & Zoonotic Disease Control**:  
   - Molecular diagnostics, parasitology, and pharmacovigilance for veterinary drugs.  
4. **Ethical & Societal Impact**:  
   - Critical evaluation of biotechnological innovations on animal welfare, biodiversity, and public health.  

---

#### **Learning Outcomes (Master’s Competencies)**  
| **Descriptor**               | **Key Skills**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **I. Critical Judgment**     | Design research, analyze operational challenges, assess ethical/societal impacts of biotech innovations. |
| **II. Communication**        | Present complex scientific concepts to specialists and non-specialists (e.g., industry, policymakers). |
| **III. Autonomous Learning** | Conduct independent research using digital databases, update professional knowledge via continuous learning. |
| **IV. Professional Application** | Apply biotech tools in diagnostics, therapeutics, and biodiversity preservation. |

---

#### **Teaching & Assessment Methods**  
- **Practical Training**: Lab work, internships in biotech firms, diagnostic labs, and pharmaceutical industries.  
- **Exams**: Written/oral tests, technical reports, presentations (using digital tools).  
- **Workshops & Seminars**: Collaborative projects, case studies on real-world biotech challenges.  

---

#### **Professional Roles (Post-Graduation)**  
| **Role**                     | **Key Responsibilities**                                                                 |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Therapeutic Specialist**   | Develop and test novel therapeutics for animal diseases; use animal models in biomedical research. |
| **Project Manager**          | Manage R&D projects, patent development, and industrial applications of diagnostic/therapeutic tools. |
| **Diagnostic Expert**        | Operate molecular diagnostics, analyze genetic variability, and monitor zoonotic disease spread. |
| **Biodiversity & Reproduction Specialist** | Preserve endangered species, optimize breeding programs, and ensure genetic diversity in livestock. |

---

#### **Unique Program Highlights**  
- **Interdisciplinary Approach**: Combines veterinary medicine, biotechnology, ethics, and industry collaboration.  
- **Industry Alignment**: Prepares graduates for roles in biotech firms, pharmaceutical companies, diagnostic labs, and conservation organizations.  
- **Global Relevance**: Addresses zoonotic diseases, sustainable agriculture, and biodiversity loss—critical global challenges.  

---

**Target Audience**:  
Students aiming for careers in veterinary biotechnology, translational medicine, animal health innovation, and biodiversity conservation.  

**Note**: Program is taught entirely in Italian, requiring proficiency for full engagement. Graduates are equipped to contribute to both scientific advancement and societal well-being through evidence-based biotech solutions.

[2015] SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY AND SAFETY OF ANIMAL PRODUCTION Bachelor's Degree Course

-----

### **Program Summary: Sciences and Technologies of Animal Production and Food Safety**  
*(Scienze e Tecnologie delle Produzioni Animali e Sicurezza Alimentare)*  

**Degree Level**: Bachelor’s (Laurea)  
**Language of Instruction**: Italian (with mandatory English proficiency for professional communication).  

---

### **Core Focus Areas**  
This program integrates **animal production systems**, **food safety**, **quality control**, and **sustainability** across the entire food supply chain—from livestock farming to processing and distribution. Key themes include:  
- **Technical & Economic Management**: Optimizing production efficiency while ensuring hygiene and cost-effectiveness in agro-zootechnical enterprises.  
- **Food Safety & Quality**: Implementing protocols for animal welfare, product safety, and environmental impact assessment (e.g., reducing ecological footprint in production chains).  
- **Regulatory Compliance**: Adhering to EU standards for food safety (e.g., HACCP, traceability) and animal welfare regulations.  

---

### **Learning Outcomes (Dublin Descriptors)**  
Graduates will demonstrate:  
1. **Knowledge Application**: Use of scientific methods to solve technical problems in animal production and food processing (e.g., feed analysis, meat quality control).  
2. **Critical Judgment**: Ability to interpret data (lab/field) and address ethical/social issues (e.g., sustainable farming vs. resource use).  
3. **Communication**: Clear articulation of technical concepts to both specialists (e.g., industry partners) and non-specialists (e.g., consumers).  
4. **Lifelong Learning**: Capacity to adapt to evolving industry standards through continuous education (e.g., EU food safety updates).  

---

### **Practical Training**  
- **Internships (Stage)**: Mandatory placements in:  
  - Animal farms, slaughterhouses, and food processing plants (e.g., dairies, meat factories).  
  - Quality control labs (testing feed, raw materials, and final products).  
  - Public/private research institutions.  
- **Simulations & E-Learning**: Virtual tools for scenario-based problem-solving (e.g., outbreak management in food supply chains).  

---

### **Career Opportunities**  
Graduates qualify for roles in:  
- **Production & Processing**:  
  - *Quality Manager* (e.g., in cheese factories, salumerie).  
  - *Animal Welfare Officer* (safeguarding humane practices during slaughter).  
  - *Technical Advisor* for feed companies or livestock farms.  
- **Regulation & Certification**:  
  - *Supply Chain Auditor* (certifying production chains for safety/compliance).  
  - *Food Safety Specialist* in retail (e.g., large supermarkets, distributors).  
- **Research & Innovation**:  
  - Roles in public/private R&D centers (e.g., developing eco-friendly feed, renewable energy from agricultural waste).  

---

### **Professional Classification**  
Aligned with Italian professional categories:  
- **3.1**: Technical roles in scientific/engineering fields (e.g., food technology).  
- **3.2**: Technical roles in health/safety (e.g., food safety management).  

---

### **Why This Program?**  
- **Holistic Approach**: Bridges animal husbandry, food safety, and sustainability—addressing modern industry demands.  
- **Industry Relevance**: Directly prepares students for EU-regulated roles in a $1.5T global food sector.  
- **Global Readiness**: English proficiency ensures competitiveness in international markets (e.g., EU export standards).  

*Note: Graduates may pursue master’s degrees in food science, veterinary medicine, or agricultural economics for advanced roles.*  

---  
**Ideal for**: Students passionate about ethical food systems, animal welfare, and the science behind safe, sustainable food production. 🌱🐄🔬
